deferred.detail:
`js/display.js flush_screen()` calls `_buildScreenOutput()`, which clears the
terminal and repaints from `game.level`. `display.c`'s writes only the glyph
buffer entries whose `gnew` is set and never clears, and `select_menu()` sets
`gb.bot_disabled` so `bot()` is skipped while a menu owns the screen.

That difference became reachable when `js/getline.js` ported
`pline.c vpline()`'s `if (u.ux) flush_screen(...)`, which the `#` prompt
genuinely needs. The call is faithful; the function it calls is not. At the two
pre-existing menu-search call sites the rebuild erases the open menu, and the
correctness pass over `60bf3d0..f826ba5` reproduced it end to end.

`.agents/review.md` puts this outside audit-fix scope: it changes rendering
behavior and needs a mechanism the port lacks. Do not paper over it by dropping
the `flush_screen(1)` call, which `vpline()` really does make. Port the `gnew`
dirty discipline and `gb.bot_disabled` so `flush_screen()` repaints only changed
cells, then satisfy the readiness note again and run a new full correctness pass
over the expanded range, as that file requires.

**Every extended-command goal depends on this one.** Thirteen of the
thirty-three development sessions stop on an extended command: five on
`#levelchange`, two on `#ride`, and one each on `#loot`, `#name`, `#chat`,
`#twoweapon`, `#pray` and `#wizwish`. Each draws a prompt or a menu into the two
defects recorded here. `scripts/scan-debt.mjs` now ranks `#levelchange` first at
188 screens of `unlocks` and `#ride` second at 92, so the dependency is live
rather than deferred. Whoever takes either goal reads this entry first and
decides whether the prompt it draws reaches the menu-erasure path.

**What is now known about which goals it blocks.** Two traces settle more than
the caution above implies.

`goto_level()` calls `docrt()` (`do.c`, 363 lines into the function, commented
"does a full vision recalc"), so C repaints the whole screen on the
level-transition path. The port's always-full repaint coincides with C's there.
The descent goal does **not** wait on this entry. What the descent goal does owe
it is separate: `goto_level()` calls `flush_screen(-1)` twice, at 243 and 364,
where `-1` postpones the map flush, and the port has no notion of postponing
one. That is an ordering question for the descent goal to trace. This defect
does not own it.

The `#ride` goal's slice 1 drew a `getdir()` prompt straight at this defect and
it did not fire: all 11 matrix segments matched cell for cell. Both known
victims are menu *search* prompts, so the reachable surface is narrower than
this entry first suggested.

`#levelchange` is the goal that should not start before this lands. It sits at
128 `unlocks` across five sessions and draws both a prompt and a menu into the
two recorded victims.

`scripts/score-baseline.mjs` changes what the conversion costs to attempt. The
worry below is that `_buildScreenOutput()` is the port's only map renderer,
behind all eleven `flush_screen()` call sites, so converting it puts every
matching screen at risk. A regression used to surface as a total someone had to
examine per session; the ratchet now fails `npm run checkpoint` and names the
sessions that dropped.

Three findings from that pass are the same defect seen from three angles: the
menu erasure itself, the two menu call sites left untested against it, and the
missing `state === game` guard that the other port of the same C line carries.
A fourth, `clearMessageWindow()` blanking map rows where C repaints them
through `docorner()`, shares the cause and belongs with them.

This is a goal of its own, not a slice of the extended-command goal. Its
upstream owners are `display.c flush_screen()` (2207-2266) with the
`gbuf_start[]`/`gbuf_stop[]` bounding box that `show_glyph()`, `cls()` and the
`reset_glyph_bbox` macro maintain; `windows.c select_menu()` (1855-1865) and
`getlin()` (1867-1901), which save, set and restore `gb.bot_disabled`; and
`botl.c bot()` and `timebot()`, whose early returns read it. None of that is in
`cmd.c`, `extcmdlist[]`, or `win/tty/getline.c`; the `#` prompt is a witness
rather than the owner, and the two victims in `js/tty_menu.js` predate it.

Size it as a goal with a checklist. `_buildScreenOutput()` in
`js/display.js:2799-2863` is the port's only map renderer, behind `docrt()` and
all eleven `flush_screen()` call sites, so converting it to per-cell
`print_glyph` puts every currently matching screen at risk. It is not urgent:
it owns no fail-closed boundary, and every one of the 398 emitted screens
matches today, so nothing is emitted-and-wrong.

Second reading: Core defect and all four movements verified. _buildScreenOutput() at js/display.js:3948 still calls display.clearScreen() (:3961) and repaints from game.level, and both menu-search prompts still reach it (js/tty_menu.js:1037 and :1281 call tty_getlin, and js/getline.js:157 is `if (state.u?.ux) await flush_screen(1);`). (c) `grep -rn "await flush_screen(" js/*.js` returns 18 lines, one of which (js/display.js:4022) is inside a comment: 17, not eleven. The unmet half is genuine: flush_screen() clears gnew at js/display.js:4069-4071 but _buildScreenOutput() never reads it, and `grep -rn "function show_glyph" js/` returns only show_glyph_cell at js/display.js:1395.

deferred.id: two more gaps on the same wrapped top line
deferred.detail:
The `clearMessageWindow()` finding folded into the entry above is not alone on
the row a wrapped prompt spills onto. Two further divergences land on the same
screen, and none of the three can be validated against a C recording without
the other two, because one prompt longer than the terminal row exercises them
together.

- `topl_putsym()`'s newline arm ports the `cl_end()` at `topl.c:322` and drops
  the one at `topl.c:340`, where `if (cw->curx == 0) cl_end()` wipes the whole
  row it moved onto, so the old map row stays visible to the right of a wrapped
  prompt.
- `ttyDisplay->toplin` never takes `TOPLINE_SPECIAL_PROMPT`, which C assigns at
  `getline.c:56`. Its readers at `topl.c:139`, `155` and `163` are each gated on
  a nonzero `ttyDisplay->cury`, so the missing state first matters on that same
  wrapped line.

Both sites now say in a comment what they omit and why. Fix them with the
`flush_screen()` goal, then record a differential for a prompt longer than 78
characters. `scripts/run-extended-command-prompt.mjs` stops one character short
of that wrap deliberately: `hooked_tty_getlin()`'s `BUFSZ` and `COLNO` length
cap sits beyond it and stays unreachable until this lands.

The other eight findings the pass recorded at `e892300` deferred are closed at
the commit that added this entry: four comments now describe the code they sit
on, and four tests now fail against the mutations they were supposed to catch —
`doextcmd()`'s default arm, the generated table's unpinned rows and flag values,
`##` recursion, and the input-length segment.

The pass record in `QUALITY.json` has one imprecision worth knowing when reading
it: its `productionDefects` list names the two `flush_screen()` companions but
omits the `clearMessageWindow()` defect above, listing a test finding in its
place. The counts are right and the ledger is append-only, so the correction
lives here rather than in the record.

`display.c newsym()` has an out-of-sight arm that shows a monster when
`see_with_infrared(mon) && mon_visible(mon)`; `js/display.js newsym()` does not.
Reproduce with seed 7000063, a female chaotic orcish Rogue, moves `" L"`: C's
mid-run animation frames show `r` at `<11,13>`, a square the hero could see but
cannot, and the port leaves it blank.

The room-run slice found this and left it, because `newsym()` is load-bearing
for every screen the port draws and the slice's own boundary did not need it.
That case is deliberately absent from `scripts/run-room-runs.mjs`. Fix it with
the infravision work rather than inside a movement slice.

deferred.id: vision_recalc(2) skips the redraw C performs
deferred.detail:
`js/vision.js vision_recalc()` guards its main update loop at `js/vision.js:746`
so that `control === 2` skips it. C does not: at that control value it still
walks every previously visible cell calling `newsym()`, then calls
`newsym(u.ux, u.uy)` and `notice_all_mons(TRUE)` on the way out. The port
therefore leaves the left level's remembered glyphs as they were.

The descent goal's slice 2 connected the only caller that passes 2,
`goto_level()`'s call at `do.c:1631`, and left the gap unfixed deliberately.
Nothing flushes the screen between that call and slice 2's refusal, and slice 3
repaints through `docrt()` regardless, so no screen the port draws today can
show the difference.

It becomes reachable at slice 4, the restore path, which re-reads the glyphs
this call was supposed to update. Fix it with `getlev()`, or sooner if another
caller passes 2.

deferred.id: an indented inverse menu heading cannot match
deferred.detail:
The spell menu's column header records as `\x1b[20C\x1b[7m    Name`: C moves
the cursor to the window edge, turns inverse video on, prints four spaces, then
prints `Name`. `serialize()` in `frozen/terminal.js`, which the judge
substitutes for `js/terminal.js`, finds the first cell in the row whose
character is not a space and emits the cursor-forward jump ahead of any SGR
sequence, so those four cells decode as default-attribute spaces. The scorer
does not forgive that: `SPACE_VISIBLE_ATTRS` in `frozen/screen-decode.mjs`
counts inverse and underline as visible on a space, so `diffCell()` reports
`attr` and the screen misses on four cells.

Twelve recorded screens across nine development sessions carry that heading,
every one of them a spell list under the default
`menu_headings:[no-color&inverse]`. A heading whose text starts at a glyph, such
as the options menu's `General`, is unaffected, which is why the inventory menu
matches. The `+` segments added to `scripts/run-no-time-commands.mjs` at
`ff6efb9` set `menu_headings:none` to sidestep it.

No fix in game code exists, because `AGENTS.md` requires leaving
`js/terminal.js` unchanged and the judge replaces it regardless. Treat it as a
ceiling: a session that displays the spell menu under the default option loses
that screen however faithful the port is.

notes.text: Correction, verified at source: this entry names the options menu's General heading as an example of the UNAFFECTED case, and it is the affected one. options.c:8584 is Sprintf(buf, " %-30s ", OptS_type[section]) -- the heading string begins with a literal space, so the highlighted run starts one column before the first glyph, exactly like the spell menu's four spaces. Measured rather than argued during the options-simple-menu goal: a default-heading recording differs from the port on precisely row 4 col 1 and row 9 col 1 of page 1 and the two equivalents on page 2, and nowhere else. The consequence is a ceiling nobody had counted: over seed0006's stretch, 15 of the 28 forecast steps carry such a cell and can never match, so that goal's real ceiling is 13. The unaffected example is doset()'s own headings, which start at a glyph, and that is why the inventory menu matches. Whoever revisits this entry should also revisit any forecast that leaned on the original wording.

Second correction, verified at this note's commit, and a warning about reading order. The `detail` above offers the options menu's `General` heading as the example of a heading that is UNAFFECTED because its text starts at a glyph. The first note refutes exactly that, citing options.c:8584's Sprintf(buf, " %-30s ", OptS_type[section]): the string begins with a literal space, so the heading is affected. A reader who stops at `detail` takes away the wrong example. The ledger writes `detail` once and never rewrites it, so the entry's current claim is `detail` as amended by both notes, and the unaffected example is doset()'s own headings, which do start at a glyph -- the reason the inventory menu matches.

The mechanism in `detail` is also narrower than the defect. It says serialize() "emits the cursor-forward jump ahead of any SGR sequence", which cannot explain a one-space indent, because no jump is emitted for one. frozen/terminal.js:683-684 emits \x1b[${firstCol}C only when firstCol > 4 and ' '.repeat(firstCol) otherwise. Both arms sit ahead of the SGR loop at :685-693, so both lose the attribute on every leading space.

Reproduced for this note against frozen/terminal.js and frozen/screen-decode.mjs, writing " General" with ATR_INVERSE at row 0 and comparing the grid with decodeScreen(serialize()): an indent of 1 differs in 1 cell and serializes as " \x1b[7;37mGeneral"; 4 differs in 4 and takes the same literal-space arm; 5 differs in 5 and 20 in 20, both taking the \x1b[NC arm. One lost cell per leading space, whichever arm runs. The ceiling is therefore any highlighted run beginning with a space, at any indent, not only the spell menu's four.

Reported upstream as davidbau/teleport-contest issue 18, "serialize() discards the attributes of a row's leading spaces", filed 12 August 2026. The issue carries a rendered before-and-after of seed0200 step 30, the count of affected screens across the starter skeleton's own sessions, and the contradiction with the equality contract at docs/API.md:272-276. Measured for it: 12 of the 33 sessions under sessions/ hold 34 affected screens and lose 92 cells. The options menu accounts for 22 of those screens at one cell per section heading, through serialize()'s padding branch; the spell menu accounts for 12 at four cells each, through its cursor-forward branch. The ceiling stands until a corrected scorer runs, and the two candidate fixes move different sets of published scores, so neither is backward-compatible with the recorded corpus.

Priced at e2cbafd during goal selection. The capping subagent found seed0006 carries 8 wrong screens today, indices 49 and 57-63, every one an options-menu screen failing on one cell: C sets attr 1 on the leading space at column 1 of each section-heading row and the port's bold run starts one cell late. It read those 8 as recoverable by porting the options menu and priced that candidate at 31 plus 8. The goal-selector corrected it: those screens are this entry, the padding branch of frozen/terminal.js serialize() at 679-693, which emits the leading-space jump ahead of the SGR loop. frozen/ is judge-substituted and AGENTS.md forbids changing js/terminal.js, so no port recovers them; it is filed upstream as davidbau/teleport-contest issue 18. One limit on that correction, stated by the selector rather than hidden: it verified the port's grid is bit-identical to C for the spell-menu case at seed0016 and seed0200, cells {ch:' ', color:8, attr:1}, but did not verify the grid for seed0006's options-menu case, relying on this entry's own note attributing it to the padding branch. Run that grid check before pricing those 8 as recoverable.

deferred.id: Monnam() has no do_it branch, so an unspottable monster gets a name
deferred.detail:
C's `x_monnam()` returns `"it"` when `canspotmon()` is false and the article is
not `ARTICLE_YOUR` (`do_name.c:863`, `876-882`). `js/do_name.js`'s
`monsterCommonName()` and `capitalizedMonsterName()` have no such branch and
never consult visibility, so every message that names a monster the hero cannot
spot answers the species name where C answers `It`.

This is a **silent divergence, not a refusal**: nothing stops, and the first
evidence would be a screen mismatch. `js/trap_effects.js thitm()` is one
reachable writer, through `pline_mon(mon, "%s is almost hit by %s!",
Monnam(mon), ...)` at `trap.c:6732-6734`, and there will be others as combat
lands.

Nothing on dungeon level one sets `minvis`, and `assertSimpleActionState()`
refuses `is_hider`, so no admitted path reaches it today. It was found by a
test that made a monster `minvis` to separate two visibility gates and pinned
the species name as correct; that fixture now grants detection instead, which
keeps `canspotmon()` true, and `scripts/monmove.test.mjs` asserts both gates
directly. Port the `do_it` branch with the goal that first admits an
unspottable monster, and give it the mirror case.

The correctness pass over `06a5629..bf96cda` confirmed sixteen findings; three
were applied at `8de4b76` and thirteen are recorded here.

**Assertions that do not discriminate**, each verified by mutation with the
suite green: neither diagonal-doorway predicate's `PASSES_WALLS` guard is
covered, and the test claiming to cover `cant_squeeze_thru()`'s four results
never takes its `passes_walls` early return; `floor_trigger()`'s fourteen-case
table has no direct test; `check_in_air()`'s `trflags` arms are unreachable
from every ported caller; five of `TRAP_NOTE_NAMES`' twelve entries are pinned
by neither the suite nor the matrix; the `tt === HOLE && !mindless()` half of
`already_seen` is reachable at depth one and untested; nothing pins
`mon_learns_traps()` and `mons_see_trap()` to their position after
`mintrap()`'s two early returns, so hoisting them above the gates passes; and
**nothing in the repository distinguishes `mons_see_trap()` from a no-op** —
deleting its only call site leaves the whole suite green.

**A second owner for one C state value.** `mon_learns_traps()` is now the
port's owner of the `mtrapseen` mask, but `js/shknam.js:232` still writes the
`ALL_TRAPS` sentinel by hand as `shk.mtrapseen = -1`, where `shknam.c:669`
calls `mon_learns_traps(shk, ALL_TRAPS)`. The encoding is a port choice — C
assigns `~0L` to an unsigned field — so the two spellings agree only by
coincidence, and the shopkeeper's mask is the one value a digest would notice.

**Comments that misdescribe their code:** `postmov()`'s coverage list is in C's
execution order except for `mintrap()`; its header claims an `unsupported`
refusal for `vamp_shift()` sequencing that exists nowhere; `js/trap_effects.js`'s
header states a five-owner env contract that omits `unsupported` and `random`;
and the comment replacing the deleted trap refusal in
`js/unported_monster_actions.js` says `postmov()` calls `mintrap()` "after the
move, and only there", which is false.

deferred.id: the planning clone leaks by omission, and should be made loud or removed
deferred.detail:
`planningState()` in `js/unported_monster_actions.js` builds a copy of the game
state so `preflightSimpleMonsterActions()` can dry-run a whole monster turn
before it happens for real. The dry run has to consume the identical PRNG
stream the live pass will consume, and write nothing live. It is a port-side
invention: C never needs it, because C implements everything and never asks
whether it can support a turn.

**The evidence.** `QUALITY.json` records **nine** production defects in this
construct, across passes from `e30ea05` onward — monster-vital state, the
light-source refusal, the `minLiquid` stub, an unconverted refusal class, the
object discovery ledger, a spread that dropped eight non-enumerable catalog
aliases, a 6.4 ms per turn cost from fixing that spread by materializing, a
restore that set live `vision_full_recalc`, and `level.traps`. Two of the nine
were introduced by the fix for a previous one. No other construct in this
repository comes close.

**Why it keeps happening.** Isolation is opt-in and silent when omitted.
`planningState()` spreads the live state and then names about thirty fields to
copy; anything a new action writes that is not on that list is shared by
reference, and nothing fails. There is no upstream source to check the list
against, because the construct has no C counterpart — so a reviewer cannot
derive the correct answer, only notice the symptom. Every one of the nine was
found by symptom.

**Options, costed against measurement.** The figures below were measured on
this machine against the fixture the tests use, not estimated.

1. *Freeze the live state during planning.* Deep-freeze what the dry run can
   reach, so a leaked write throws at the leaking line instead of diverging
   silently. **It cannot run in production.** `Object.freeze()` is
   irreversible, so a frozen game cannot run the live pass that follows; the
   reversible substitute, `defineProperty({writable: false})` per property
   undone afterwards, measured 74 to 131 ms per turn against the 1.13 ms
   preflight it would guard. That is an order of magnitude worse than the
   6.4 ms catalog copy this construct was already forced to withdraw. It is
   also a weaker detector than first claimed. Of the nine, **five are not live
   writes at all** -- a missing refusal, a permissive stub, an unconverted
   refusal class, a clone that was too isolated rather than too little, and the
   6.4 ms materialization cost. Four are live writes, and the detector catches
   **three of those four**. The fourth, the restore that left live
   `vision_full_recalc` set, escapes because it is a root field the scan's own
   restore has to write, so no freeze can tell that write from a leak.
2. *Copy-on-write.* Put the planned state behind a proxy whose writes land on
   an overlay, so isolation is the default and the field list disappears. This
   was costed as the more expensive option; measuring option 1 removes that
   reason. Proxy overhead on this path has not been measured, so it is
   unranked on cost rather than preferred, but it is now the only candidate
   that could plausibly run per turn.
3. *Journal and roll back.* Run against the live state, record every mutation,
   undo on refusal. Removes the clone, but replaces one omission problem with
   another: an unrecorded mutation is exactly as silent as an uncopied field.

**What landed.** Option 1 as a test-only detector, which is where its cost
disappears and its irreversibility stops mattering:
`scripts/planning-isolation-test-support.mjs` freezes the live graph and five
cases run the dry run against it -- an ordinary move, a door opening, a pet
pickup on each of `distant_name()`'s two branches, and one burdened turn that
reaches the once-per-turn planning round through `moveloop_core()`. Each was
confirmed by a distinct mutation to `planningState()`. It found a tenth leak on
its first run: `gd` was shared, and `distant_name()` raises `gd.distantname`
through `dog_invent()`. That is balanced by its own `finally` and `gd` is
absent from a fresh game, so it was invisible both to inspection and to every
oracle; it leaks only once a live `distant_name()` has created `gd`. Fixed in
the same change.

Two exclusions are permanent and declared at the site. The live root stays
writable because the scan's own `finally` restore writes three fields on it.
The object catalog stays writable because the clone delegates to it with
`Object.create()`, and `[[Set]]` cannot shadow a frozen inherited property --
freezing it would report the copy's writes as live leaks.

**What the detector still cannot see.** `vision.c`'s module-level transparency
index (`viz_clear`, `left_ptrs`, `right_ptrs`) is not reachable from the state,
so no freeze reaches it; it stays covered by the `finally` restore and the
refusing `visionRecalc` owner. The three root fields that restore writes --
`_viz_rmin`, `_viz_rmax` and `vision_full_recalc` -- are uncovered for the same
reason, and the last of those is a recorded defect, so a dedicated case pins it
instead.

Two claims made here earlier were wrong and are corrected. `liveVisionBuffers`
*is* reachable: `js/vision.js:791` assigns `game.viz_array =
liveVisionBuffers.rows[0]`. What hid it was that its rows are `Uint8Array`, and
`Object.freeze()` throws on a typed array with elements, so the detector skipped
the views. It now snapshots every reachable view before the dry run and compares
afterwards, which catches a per-cell vision write -- confirmed by injecting one.
And a leak that *adds* a field does not escape: `Object.freeze()` already clears
`[[Extensible]]`, so an added field throws wherever the object is frozen. The
one place it can still happen is the live root, which is deliberately left
extensible, and `assertNoLeak()` checks the root's key set for exactly that.

**When.** Option 2 is not urgent by the usual test: the construct owns no
fail-closed boundary and the score is correct today. The detector removes the
reason it was urgent, by making the next omission fail loudly in the suite
rather than surface as a screen mismatch several goals later. Take option 2
when a leak escapes the five cases above, or when the field list next grows.

`AUTOUNLOCK_APPLY_KEY`, and `js/options.js` keeps an explicit setting as raw
text rather than parsing `optfn_autounlock`. The closed-door seam therefore
refuses on any explicit setting.

That is wider than it needs to be in one direction: C treats `!autounlock` as
the default, so a session setting it would run identically and the port stops
instead. Porting the parser is the fix, and it belongs with `pick_lock()` and
`autokey()`, which are what the flag selects between.

deferred.id: the postmov minvis redraw has no case that can reach it
deferred.detail:
`monmove.c postmov()` (1683-1687) repeats `newsym()` — and `see_wsegs()` for a
long worm — after the object arm whenever `mtmp->minvis` is set, whether or not
`mpickstuff()` took anything. `postSimpleMove()` in
`js/unported_monster_actions.js` omits it. Porting the arm is three lines;
recording a differential for it is what fails.

Nothing behind the current boundary sets `minvis` on D:1.

- `pm_invisible()` (mondata.h:192) covers only the stalker and the black light,
  difficulty 9 and 7. `rndmonst_adj()` caps generation at
  `monmax_difficulty(levdif) = (levdif + u.ulevel) / 2` (monst.h:259), which is
  1 on D:1 at experience level 1 and admits a black light only from level 13.
  No `dat/` Lua file names either species, and no `mkclass()` caller passes
  `S_LIGHT` or `S_ELEMENTAL`, so the cap-skipping `rn2(2)` arm at
  `makemon.c:1944` cannot reach them either.
- `MM_MINVIS` has one C caller, `read.c:3313`, behind wizard `^G`.
- The two routes that do fire in C on D:1 at experience level 1 are each
  refused earlier by the port. A monster that picks up a randomly generated
  cloak of invisibility wears it on its next turn through
  `movemon_singlemon()` → `m_dowear()` → `update_mon_extrinsics()`
  (worn.c:598); the port refuses `monster equipment changes` before that runs.
  A monster that quaffs a potion of invisibility reaches `mon_set_minvis()`
  through `muse.c use_misc()`; `js/muse.js` ports the selection and refuses
  `monster item use` before the effect.

The arm is therefore dormant behind two refusals rather than silently wrong,
and `AGENTS.md`'s rule to identify where the running game will use a piece of
code before writing it defers it. Port it with whichever of monster equipment
changes or monster item use lands first, and record the differential then.

One latent trap belongs with it. `updateMonsterArmorEffects()` at
`js/makemon_create.js:1606` implements only `MUMMY_WRAPPING` and `SPEED_BOOTS`
and omits `update_mon_extrinsics()`'s `INVIS` arm silently rather than
refusing. The post-creation wear path is masked by the boundary above, but the
creation path calls the same function, so a creation-time cloak of invisibility
would diverge without erroring. No creation-time route grants one today.

deferred.id: the planning clone's object copy is still expensive
deferred.detail:
One symptom of the mechanism described under `### Planning clone` above; fix
it there rather than in isolation if that plan is taken.

`cloneObjects()` builds each copy with `newObject({ ...original })`, which
constructs a 60-field default and installs 16 alias accessors before
overwriting them. Measured at 27-38 microseconds per object, about 0.9 ms per
turn. Hoisting the alias descriptors to module scope and using
`Object.defineProperties()` measured 2.2 times cheaper, and `Object.create()`
was below timer resolution.

The catalog copy beside it was fixed this way already: it had cost 6.4 ms per
elapsed turn, 80-92% of a scored turn, and prototype delegation removed that at
no correctness cost. The same treatment probably suits the object copy, but it
needs its own check, because unlike a catalog entry an object is written
through more paths.

That catalog fix left one loose end: `js/unported_monster_actions.js:85` still
imports `copyObjclassEntry`, which no line of the file calls now that the
catalog clone is `state.objects?.map((entry) => Object.create(entry))`. Delete
the import with the next simplification pass.

The correctness pass over `4d54fa8..2776192` confirmed ten findings; two were
applied and eight are recorded here. The applied pair are described in
`SCORE.md` at the fix commit; these are what remains.

They divide into assertions that do not discriminate — the new diagonal arms,
the consolidated `cant_squeeze_thru()` and the obstacle-arm ordering each have
coverage that survives mutation — and comments that overstate what their code
establishes. Two vision comments in `js/unported_monster_actions.js` also
remain unsettled: the slice worker declined to invent a justification it could
not derive, and the pass did not settle them either.

Take them with whatever next reads `test_move()`; none owns a fail-closed
boundary today.

The correctness pass over `c706db8..06a5629` confirmed ten findings; two were
applied and eight are recorded here. Most concern the vision isolation the
slice built as a precondition.

**The isolation's own seams.**

- `isolatePlannedVision()` guards the cloned terrain grid behind
  `state._visionBuffers`, so two unrelated isolations share one early return.
  Nothing sets that field early today — the adjudicator confirmed it is written
  in exactly one place, after both isolations — but a later change that
  allocates planning buffers first would silently leave `level.locations`
  pointing at the live array, and `postmov()` writes `D_ISOPEN` through it.
  Give the two isolations independent guards.
- No test plans two door openings in one scan, so the private COULD_SEE buffer
  pair the settled design rests on is never exercised twice.
- The transparency-index restore is in a `finally` specifically so it runs
  after a refusal, and no test covers the refusal path: moving the restore out
  of the `finally` leaves the suite green.
- `visionSnapshot()` and `preflightSnapshot()` omit `game.vision_full_recalc`,
  which is how the leak fixed at this cycle's head stayed invisible.

**Comments that outlived their code.** The third is closed at the commit that
added this sentence: `admitDoorOpening()` refuses nothing — it only isolates
the planning vision buffers — and two segments of
`scripts/run-monster-door-open.mjs` do record a hero watching a monster open a
door, so `scripts/monmove.test.mjs` now names the recorded evidence for the
first arm and the invisible-monster reason the second has none. Two remain,
and both need a re-derived justification rather than a reworded one:
`planningEveryTurnEffect()`'s refusal cites a guard in `rebuildVisionPoint()`
that this same range deleted, and `planSimpleMonsterScan()`'s `visionRecalc`
refusal still says the dry run cannot reproduce the live buffers, which
`planningVisionRecalc()` now does. Both refusals may well still be right; what
is missing is the evidence for why, and inventing one would be worse than the
stale text.

**One production gap.** `refuseHeroAttack()` gates on
`monnear(monster, monster.mux, monster.muy)`, C's `range2` — whether the
monster *thinks* it is near — where the arm it stands in front of needs the
real position. It belongs with the combat work that already owns
`refuseHeroAttack()`'s missing `find_offensive()` path.

above, that a monster which moves and then throws diverges silently with no

deferred.id: the planning clone must copy non-enumerable catalog aliases
deferred.detail:
One of the nine defects counted under `### Planning clone` above, kept here for
the general trap it records: a spread is not a copy when the source uses
`Object.defineProperty`.

`js/objects.js defineObjclassAliases()` installs eight aliases — `oc_skill`,
`oc_armcat`, `a_ac`, `a_can`, `oc_bimanual`, `oc_bulky`, `oc_hitbon` and
`oc_level` — as non-enumerable properties, so a spread copy silently drops
them. `planningState()` cloned the catalog with `{ ...entry }` from `8bd4d6a`
until `39e5df1`, which meant the dry run read `undefined` for all eight and
took different branches from the live pass.

`copyObjclassEntry()` in `js/objects.js` is the correct way to *materialize* a
copy of a catalog entry, and the generator emits it. The planning clone no
longer needs one: it uses `Object.create(entry)` prototype delegation, which
gave the same isolation without the 6.4 ms per turn a 482-entry copy cost. The
import in `js/unported_monster_actions.js` is dead as a result and is left for
a simplification pass. The general lesson is recorded here
because the same trap applies to any state the port clones: a spread is not a
copy when the source uses `Object.defineProperty`.

`UnsupportedMonsterCreationError` is listed in

identical output. Converting on the live path alone would not be enough,
because moves and the regeneration draws are already spent by then, so the fix
is a preflight for the unburdened path, as `preflightGetHungry()` and
`preflight_nh_timeout_elapsed_turn()` already do for theirs.

deferred.id: go.occupation has one writer and three readers that never see it
deferred.detail:
`js/cmd.js set_occupation()` stores C's `go.occupation` at
`state.go.occupation`. The three JavaScript readers that already stood for that
C value read `state.occupation`, which nothing in `js/` assigns:
`grep -rn "\.occupation" js/` returns `js/monmove.js:529` and `:555`,
`js/unported_monster_actions.js:871` and `js/teleport.js:259` as the readers of
the bare name, and no assignment to it anywhere. Every writer of the value
names `state.go.occupation`: `js/cmd.js:180` installs one, and `js/eat.js:1221`
and `js/allmain.js:877` clear it.

The reader that matters is `monmove.c dochugw()` (213, 223-235), which calls
`stop_occupation()` when a hostile, spottable monster is within
`(BOLT_LIM + 1)^2` and either could not be seen before or was further away. C
therefore prints "You stop eating the food ration." and abandons the meal
several turns before the monster becomes adjacent. The port evaluates a falsy
`state.occupation`, short-circuits, and eats on to "You finish eating the food
ration." `moveloop_core()`'s own `monster_nearby()` test does not cover the
gap, because `hack.c monster_nearby()` (4106-4127) scans the eight adjacent
squares alone. This is a **silent divergence, not a refusal**: the fail-closed
stop the port installed for it,
`js/unported_monster_actions.js:797 stopOccupation`, can never run.

The correctness pass over `02c6e59..dc4e009` confirmed it and the audit fix at
that pass left it here, because repointing the readers changes a state owner
and makes a previously dead refusal live, which `.agents/review.md` puts
outside audit-fix scope. Two parts need a decision rather than a rename.
`js/unported_monster_actions.js:871` refuses the elapsed-turn monster scan
outright, so wiring it up unchanged would refuse every occupation turn;
`grep -n occupation nethack-c/upstream/src/allmain.c` returns only lines 332,
485-506 and 684-689, so C gates nothing in that block on `go.occupation` and
the term is stale scaffolding. `js/makemon_create.js:2484` documents
`makemon.c:1503`'s `if (go.occupation) dochugw(mtmp, FALSE)` as deferred and is
the same missing wiring.

Fix it with a fresh differential: a recorded case where a hostile monster first
enters the nine-square window mid-meal, which shows C printing "You stop
eating ..." on that turn. Guard the result with a repository-wide grep that
every reader names one field. Also correct the `stop_occupation()`
reachability row in the slice's checklist, which omits `monmove.c dochugw()`
and `makemon.c:1503`.

deferred.id: the status line repaints on every turn, where C gates it
deferred.detail:
`allmain.c moveloop_core()` (473-478) repaints the status line only when a
writer has marked it dirty: `if (disp.botl || disp.botlx) { bot();
curs_on_u(); } else if (disp.time_botl) { timebot(); curs_on_u(); }`, and
`botl.c timebot()` refreshes `BL_TIME` alone through `stat_update_time()`, so
the hunger cell keeps its last rendered text. `js/allmain.js:831` runs
`find_ac(g); await bot(); await flush_screen(1);` with no gate at all.

That became observable when the occupation landed. `eat.c newuhs()`'s
`if (go.occupation == eatfood || gf.force_save_hs)` arm assigns `u.uhs` and
returns before any `disp.botl = TRUE`, so a meal that crosses a hunger boundary
moves the status silently. Driving matrix segment 5820079 turn by turn shows
the port's last screen row carrying "Satiated" on the three turns after the
crossing while its own `disp.botl` is false, which is C's gate tracked
correctly and then ignored at the call site.

No captured screen differs today, because a mid-meal frame is captured only at
an input boundary and the two foods this slice ports cannot produce one inside
the window. A mid-meal `--More--` would: `fprefx()`'s "This satiates your
stomach!" left unseen, followed by a `dosounds()` "You hear ..." on a later
meal turn, is the reachable pairing. It would be the project's first
emitted-and-wrong screen.

The fix belongs where C puts it, in `moveloop_core()`, and needs `timebot()`
ported for the second arm. It changes rendering behavior on a line that runs
every turn of every session, so it needs its own differential and a whole-score
comparison rather than an audit fix. The cheap regression to carry with it:
assert that the last row of `game.nhDisplay.grid` holds no hunger word on the
turn after the crossing while `game.disp.botl` is false.

continued eating`, because the hero is already SATIATED when the second meal

finished." where C prints "You finish eating the cram ration."

Repairing it needs a fresh C recording, which puts it outside audit-fix scope.

meal starts, which clears both blockers at once, and give the recipe the extra
keys any `--More--` needs. Then assert that `game.nomovemsg` is null at the end
and read the final top line off the amended recording rather than assuming the

The claim that done_eating()'s nomovemsg reset is unpinned end to end is false, checked on 7 August 2026. Deleting 'state.nomovemsg = null;' at js/eat.js:1225 and running the whole suite turns exactly one test red: scripts/eat-occupation.test.mjs:246, 'done_eating leaves gn.nomovemsg in a shape its reader accepts', which replays segment 5820011 with 'ed ' and asserts game.nomovemsg is null after a first meal. Only a second meal can show the stale 'You're finally finished.' where C prints 'You finish eating the cram ration.' Closing this therefore still needs the fresh recording the entry describes -- a seed or wait count leaving the hero below SATIATED when the second meal starts -- and not a unit test.

Closed by the tests deferral burn-down. a768cc4 added loadTwoMealRecipe() to scripts/run-eat-occupation.mjs with its own runFreshMatrix() entry at chunkLimit 1, and a test in scripts/eat-occupation.test.mjs. The turn counts (T:2, T:6, T:9) and the closing line 'This pancake is delicious!  You finish eating the pancake.' in the test were read off that recording, not assumed. The commit also corrects segment 5820041's comment, which claimed the occupation was installed, run down and cleared twice; replaying it shows it stops at T:7 with victual.usedtime 0, eating 1, and slot h an unbitten cram ration.

Substitution ruled out: With the tests staged, `if (++meal.usedtime <= meal.reqtime)` in js/eat.js eatfood() was replaced by `<`, which fails the new test's T:9 assertion; and done_eating()'s `if (carried(piece)) useup(piece, env); else useupf(piece, 1, env);` pair was deleted, which fails its 'the second pancake was eaten too' assertion. Both also fail older tests in the file, because a second meal runs the same lines as the first; the segment's unique evidence is the recorded second meal itself. deferred.detail:
`scripts/score-baseline.mjs` now holds a per-session baseline of matched screens
and matched random-number values, and `npm run checkpoint` fails when a session
falls below it. This entry previously claimed the checkpoint "cannot fail on the
development score" as though a gate had been widened. That was wrong: `passed`
was the scoring script's exit code, and that script is a reporter which exits 0
whatever the score, so no predicate could have caught a regression. Nothing
compared the score to anything.

Two limits remain. The ratchet reads only the matched counts, so a change that
keeps every match and alters an unmatched screen is invisible to it. And a
correct change that adds a refusal earlier than a session's current stop lowers
that session legitimately; `score-baseline.mjs lower` records the reason beside
the number, and a pattern of lowerings against one session is worth reading as a
list.

deferred.id: recording a debug-mode session needs local setup
deferred.detail:
Two constraints bind anyone recording a `playmode:debug` case, both found while
closing the `#` prompt slice at `f826ba5`.

The recorder denies debug mode unless its `sysconf` names the running user:
`WIZARDS=root games vtjeng`. That file is gitignored and uncommitted, so a fresh
checkout does not have it. Without it the recorder falls back to explore mode
and diverges from the intended run at PRNG call 202, which looks like a port
defect rather than a setup problem.

And a debug segment cannot be followed by another segment in one recording.
`set_playmode()` renames the hero to "wizard", and `record-session.mjs`
`clearStaleState` strips those files only before a recording's first segment, so
a second debug game in the same recording dies. Record debug cases one segment
at a time; the four in `scripts/run-extended-command-prompt.mjs` are.

This matters beyond the current slice: five development sessions stop at
`wiz_level_change`, so every one of them will need debug-mode recordings.

deferred.id: a mistyped substitution name disables a test
deferred.detail:
A test substitutes its own function for a real one by naming it in the `env`
object a ported function reads:

    const erodeObject = env.erodeObject ?? erode_monster_object;

The lookup accepts any name. `erodeObj` falls through to the real
implementation, so a substitution written to fail the test if it ever runs
never runs, and the suite reports green. Only a substitution with nothing but
that tripwire is silent; one whose call is recorded and asserted afterwards
fails when its name goes stale.

Six places are confirmed, each by renaming a key and watching the suite stay
green on 29 July 2026:

| File | What is disarmed |
| --- | --- |
| `scripts/dogmove.test.mjs` | four tripwires at lines 536, 607, 713, 739; two more at 606 and 639 resolve through `js/dogmove.js` itself |
| `scripts/dogmove-inventory.test.mjs` | the `classified` guard at line 194, and `canCarry` at 347, which passes for the wrong reason |
| `scripts/dogmove-goal.test.mjs` | `couldSee` at line 672, which reaches the asserted outcome through the default |
| `scripts/monmove-items.test.mjs` | the `monsterCanSee` tripwire at line 415 |
| `scripts/monmove-dochug.test.mjs` | five tripwires; line 162 has no positive counterpart at all |
| `scripts/trap-water-damage.test.mjs` | three tripwires at lines 39, 50, 76; no helper exists, the defaults live in `js/trap_water_damage.js:17` |

`scripts/mon.test.mjs` had the same defect and `fcdca9c` fixed it, by rejecting
any override key its helper does not define.

Two mechanisms need different fixes. Where a test helper holds the defaults,
the helper rejects unknown keys. Where production resolves the operation
itself, as `js/dogmove.js:209` and `js/trap_water_damage.js:17` do, the check
belongs in production against the names that file recognises, and it must run
before the first early return: a guard placed after one leaves every path that
returns earlier unprotected.

A worked fix for `js/trap_water_damage.js` turns all three of its silent
renames into failures. It moves the two fallbacks into one frozen table, drops
the third parameter from `waterOperation()`, and calls
`requireKnownWaterOperations(env)` as the first statement of the exported
function. 28 lines added, 12 removed.

`js/dogmove.js` is harder. It resolves operations through five idioms in one
file: an object literal at lines 207-214, bare `??` at line 333, and three
lookup helpers taking the name as a string at lines 397, 455, and 830. A check
there means routing every resolution through one helper backed by one table.
Budget an afternoon.

There are 223 `?? fallback` resolutions across 49 files in `js/`. Most are
covered by no tripwire and need nothing. These seams shrink as the port
advances, so fix the proven six and leave the rest.

deferred.detail:
Riding movement and riding combat, which is where `seed0104-knight-ride-combat`
stops now. `domove()` refuses a mounted hero: C carries the steed through
`stucksteed()`, the `<mx,my>` updates, `exercise_steed()` and `u_on_newpos()`,
none ported, and that refusal costs that session nine screens it would
otherwise match. Whoever takes it inherits one traced constraint worth not
re-deriving: **only a Knight can reach a saddled steed at all.**
`dog.c:263-268` puts a saddle on a starting pet only when
`pettype == PM_PONY`, `role.c:209` gives that `petnum` to the Knight alone,
and `u.uroleplay.pauper` suppresses the saddle even then. Every other route to
a tame saddled monster needs `#apply` or a taming effect. That is why
`mount_steed()`'s `!Role_if(PM_KNIGHT)` tame decrement at `steed.c:308` has no
recordable case and is pinned by a focused test instead.

notes.text:
Three of this entry's citations have drifted, and its closing condition is not mechanical. Checked on 7 August 2026.

The run-loop re-entry is js/allmain.js:1021, not :922; line 922 is now a comment. The jsmain boundary list is js/jsmain.js:534-548, not :525-529, and it holds six classes rather than four: UnsupportedTurnBoundaryError, UnsupportedHeroMoveBoundaryError, UnsupportedHeroCommandBoundaryError, UnsupportedEarthSenseError, UnsupportedStatusRefreshError and UnsupportedSpecialRoomError. js/cmd.js:945 still calls it 'the three boundary classes', as do comments in scripts/cmd.test.mjs, scripts/wizard-level-tele.test.mjs and scripts/wizard-wish.test.mjs.

The substance holds. js/cmd.js:906 and js/allmain.js:1021 are the two live domove() call sites and neither is wrapped. Four classes reach domove() and escape runSegment() today: UnsupportedPickupError, UnsupportedFeatureDescriptionError, UnsupportedShopError and UnsupportedObjectNameError. None is one of the six, so wrapping can only convert a segment that scores zero into one that keeps its matching prefix.

The two halves are not the same size. Wrapping js/cmd.js:906 is about ten lines: executeMovement() gains a key parameter and rhack() passes the key it already holds. Wrapping js/allmain.js:1021 is a state-owner decision the entry's own text does not settle. failClosedCommand() raises UnsupportedHeroCommandBoundaryError carrying a key, which advertises a retryable keystroke; at that site rhack() is not on the stack, its finally never runs, and context.pendingCommand was deleted by the rhack() call that started the run, so no retry can honour it. The alternative with precedent is UnsupportedTurnBoundaryError, which js/allmain.js:968-978 and :450-460 already raise and which needs no key. Choosing between them decides who owns the rejected keystroke.

A fresh recording is not needed for the wrapper itself, but is needed if the implementer also retires the three ad-hoc seam guards at js/hack.js:711, :816 and :830. Those refuse before domove() runs; the wrapper refuses after domove() may have moved the hero, drawn from the PRNG and painted, so removing them reorders observable output.

The mechanics hold; three citations do not, and the closing condition has a half that is already met.

`mkbox_cnts()` is mkobj.c:303-384, not 304-382: 303 is `staticfn void` and 384 is the closing brace. Everything the entry says about its body is right -- SACK and OILSKIN_SACK fall through to `n = 1` once `svm.moves > 1` (324-331), BAG_OF_HOLDING is unconditional, and 338's `rn2(n + 1)` is therefore `rn2(2)`. `next_ident()`'s `rnd(2)` is mkobj.c:521 as cited.

`js/obj.js:1025-1054` is not the container machinery and was not when the entry was written. The switch that picks `n` and takes the `rn2(n+1)` draw is `initializeContainer()`, at js/obj.js:1128-1158 as of ea33d80, called from the two mksobj() arms below it; the loop body is `populateContainer()` in js/mkobj_container.js:153-180. Both are ports of mkbox_cnts(), split across the two files, which is worth knowing before someone looks for one function.

The refusal is `refuse('a wish for a container')` at js/objnam_readobjnam.js:1289, six lines before `mksobj()`, so nothing is drawn after the stop.

That is the problem with the closing condition. It offers "or a refusal that stops before the first divergent draw" as an alternative, and the port already satisfies it -- the refusal precedes every draw. The entry is therefore only closable on its first branch, the container reaching hold_another_object() with mkbox_cnts()'s contents, or by rewriting the condition. Whoever takes it should decide that first.

On cost: the refusal's own comment names objnam.c:5289-5299 (empty) and 5301-5310 (lock state) as what it protects, and neither applies to a plain `cursed sack`, because C gates the emptying on `d.contents == TIN_EMPTY` (5312) and the lock arm on `Is_box()` (5324). The one genuine unknown is whether all nine content classes' mksobj() tails match C; scripts/container-population.test.mjs drives only four fixed paths.

Orchestrator decision at the objects sweep, taken so no worker has to park on it: the closing condition loses its second branch. It read 'or a refusal that stops before the first divergent draw', and the note above established that the port already satisfies that, because refuse('a wish for a container') precedes every draw. Closing an entry on the very refusal that caused it would retire the record without changing the behaviour it was opened for, and this entry is the one objects deferral standing in front of a stopped session. The entry now closes only on its first branch: the wished-for container reaches hold_another_object() with the contents mkbox_cnts() gives it, matching C call for call, proved by a fresh differential. notes.text:
Both halves of this entry's central claim are false, checked on 7 August 2026.

D_BROKEN is producible by the port's generation today. rnddoor()'s five-state table reaches a real doormask through sp_lev.c lspo_door()'s coordinate arm: 4702 rolls rnddoor() for state = "random", 4721-4726 hands the roll to sel_set_door() (4646-4662), and 4660 writes it as the doormask. dat/tut-1.lua:273 is des.door({ coord = { 40,15 }, state = "random" }), which js/tutorial_level.js:460 mirrors and js/mklev.js:932-947 serves from RANDOM_SPECIAL_DOOR_STATES. Over seeds 5200001-5200060 the port's tutorial level produced D_BROKEN at map [40,15] on 11 of 60. The entry's opposite claim, and the same claim in the js/hack.js comment this commit corrects, both read lspo_door()'s room-door arm (4704-4720), which passes msk still -1 to create_door() and so discards the roll.

pick_lock() is reachable from a player command today. js/apply.js:244-251 dispatches LOCK_PICK, CREDIT_CARD and SKELETON_KEY to pick_lock(obj, 0, 0, null, state) with no refusal in front of it, and scripts/apply-lock-pick.test.mjs already drives doapply() through runSegment() for the D_ISOPEN and D_NODOOR arms.

What actually blocks the entry is that the two cannot meet. The tutorial hero enters with an empty inventory and dat/tut-1.lua places no key, lock pick or credit card. A wizard-mode hero can wish one up, but cannot walk to the broken door: a flood fill from the tutorial start over every passable square reaches 60 squares, and the only door on that region's border is dat/tut-1.lua:104's hard-coded locked door at map [5,10]. The level holds no SCORR. Passing it needs pick_lock()'s own default arm, which js/lock.js:199-200 refuses as UnsupportedLockError, or dokick.c dokick(), which has no port: grep -rn 'function dokick|dokick =' js/ returns 0. So the entry waits on the picklock() occupation, on dokick(), or on a door-breaking path that writes D_BROKEN on an ordinary dungeon level -- not on a generator that can produce the mask.

Read by the deferral staleness audit against the code at df11e8c, by one agent and then by a second asked to refute it.

First reading: The entry's own correction note (at bddc645) rests on 'dokick.c dokick(), which has no port: grep -rn \'function dokick|dokick =\' js/ returns 0'. Re-running that exact command today prints `js/dokick.js:245:export async function dokick(state = game) {`. dokick.c is now partly ported (js/dokick.js:1-16 names dokick(), kick_nondoor() and kick_dumb() as ported). The entry nonetheless stays open, because the door-breaking path is still absent: js/dokick.js:376 refuses "dokick()'s door arm, which needs kick_door()", and `grep -rn kick_door js/` finds only that refusal and two comments. blockedOn 'picklock' is also still unmet -- `grep -rn '\bpicklock\b' js/` returns only comments at js/lock.js:125 and js/lock.js:151. So no writer of D_BROKEN is reachable from a command, and js/lock.js:237-239 remains pinned by a hand-set mask alone.

Second reading: The correction the claim makes to the bddc645 note is real. That note's evidence was "dokick.c dokick(), which has no port: grep -rn 'function dokick|dokick =' js/ returns 0"; running the same command today prints `js/dokick.js:245:export async function dokick(state = game) {`, and js/dokick.js:1-3 names dokick() (1257-1470), kick_nondoor() (974-1253) and kick_dumb() (863-878) as ported. The entry still stays open for the reason given: js/dokick.js:372-377 throws UnsupportedKickError("dokick()'s door arm, which needs kick_door()") for `IS_DOOR(maploc.typ)`, and `grep -rn kick_door js/` returns only that refusal plus comments at :14 and :167. blockedOn picklock is unmet: `grep -rn '\bpicklock\b' js/` returns only js/lock.js:125 and :151, both comments. The D_BROKEN arm at js/lock.js:237-239 is still exercised only by the hand-set mask at scripts/apply-lock-pick.test.mjs:192 (`doorNorth().flags = D_BROKEN;`). One imprecision worth carrying into any note: generation can still write D_BROKEN (js/mklev.js:2678 rnddoor()), as the bddc645 note established; what is absent is a door-breaking writer reachable from a command.

Same shape as `isok-ported-twice`. A simplification pass over these two entries
would settle both.

`unportedMinliquidReason()` in `js/unported_monster_actions.js:167-168`, and
the sibling test at `:205-206`, refuse on bare `is_pool(...) || is_lava(...)`.
C's `minliquid_core()` derives the two flags with a flyer and floater
exemption:

    inpool = (is_pool(mtmp->mx, mtmp->my)
              && (!(is_flyer(mtmp->data) || is_floater(mtmp->data))
                  || Is_waterlevel(&u.uz)));            /* mon.c:967-970 */
    inlava = (is_lava(mtmp->mx, mtmp->my)
              && !(is_flyer(mtmp->data) || is_floater(mtmp->data)));

So a flying or floating monster over water or lava is left alone by C, and
refused by the port. A bat crossing a pool ends the segment where C simply
continues the turn.

The refusal is fail-closed, so it cannot produce a wrong screen or a wrong
random number; what it costs is replay length, and replay length is screens.
That makes it a scoring cost rather than a correctness defect, which is why the
gremlin slice at `3249e2d` documented it in place rather than narrowing it.

Narrowing it means porting the arms it stands in for: the drown effect at
`mon.c:1068` and the burn effect at `:1010`, with `is_flyer()` and
`is_floater()` first. Resolve this entry when those land, or earlier if a
scored session is measured stopping here on a flyer -- the cheap check is to
count how many development sessions reach a flying or floating monster over
liquid at all.

Found by reading during the `monsters` deferral sweep, not by a failing test.

deferred.detail:
`scripts/record-session.test.mjs`, "fails when a complete marker stream ends
with an unexpected signal", races. Its fake recorder writes a complete input
marker to fd 1 with `fs.writeSync(1, marker)` and then immediately runs
`process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGUSR2')`, so the parent's observation of the
marker on the pipe against its observation of the signal death is an ordering
the test does not control.

Observed once on CI during the `monsters-deferral-sweep` artifact-touch slice:
the run reported status 0 where the test asserts 1. It passes locally, and a
re-dispatch of the identical commit passed (run 31129020658, head 6b79b077), so
the failure is load-dependent rather than a defect in the recorder.

A flaky test costs more than the minutes it wastes: it teaches the next agent
to re-run a red suite instead of reading it, which is the habit most likely to
let a real regression through.

The fix is to make the ordering explicit rather than probable -- have the fake
recorder wait for the parent to acknowledge the marker before signalling, or
have the assertion accept either interleaving while still requiring the signal
to be reported. Decide which from `scripts/record-session.mjs`'s own reader,
because only one of those is faithful to what the production path guarantees.

`scripts/` is not area-owned, so this entry carries no area.

Two leftovers from the duplicate-port convergence at `1af25e7`, both found by
reading and neither in scope for that slice.

**`mwelded()` sits in the wrong file.** C owns it at `wield.c:1078`, so
`AGENTS.md` "Keep each source file's port in one place" puts it in
`js/wield.js`; the port has it at `js/weapon.js mwelded()`. The convergence
slice pointed it at the surviving `will_weld()` as its deferral asked and left
the move. The move is cheap now: `js/muse.js` and `scripts/weapon.test.mjs` are
its only importers, and the `js/weapon.js` -> `js/wield.js` import edge already
exists after the convergence. `which_armor()` is the sibling to check at the
same time, since `js/muse.js` imports both from `js/weapon.js` in one
statement.

**`_weaponInternals` is an export nobody imports.** `js/weapon.js` freezes and
exports it; `grep -rn "_weaponInternals" js/ scripts/ tools/` returns only the
definition. The convergence removed the deleted function from the object and
left the object, correctly, because deleting an export is not a rename. It is
either a test seam whose test was rewritten to import the functions directly,
or scaffolding that outlived its purpose; read `scripts/weapon.test.mjs` before
deciding which.

Neither changes behavior. Both are placement and dead-declaration cleanups of
the kind a simplification pass settles, which is why they are one entry rather
than two.

`dungeon.c depth()` has two live ports whose bodies **differ**, and one module
imports both:

- `js/dungeon.js depth(level, state = game)` threads `state`. This is the
  correct owner by file name: C defines the function in `dungeon.c`.
- `js/hacklib.js depth(uz)` ignores any state argument and reads the
  module-global `game`. `js/hacklib.js` is the wrong home, the same
  skeleton-leftover shape as the duplicate `isok()` that `1af25e7` converged.

`js/mklev.js` binds both under aliases in separate statements, `depth as
dungeon_depth` from `./dungeon.js` and `depth as depth_of_level` from
`./hacklib.js`, so a reader of either call site sees a plausible name and no
sign that two implementations are in play.

They disagree in three ways. At `js/mklev.js initialize_themeroom_branch()`,
which takes `state = game`, the `depth_of_level` call reads the level from the
passed state and `depth_start` from the module-global `game`. When
`depth_start` is 0 the `hacklib` copy returns `dlevel` through a `|| 1` and the
`dungeon` copy returns `dlevel - 1`. When the dungeon is missing the `hacklib`
copy returns a default and the `dungeon` copy throws.

This is a latent hazard rather than a demonstrated bug: no path was found today
where the passed state differs from the module global. It becomes live the
moment one does, and it will not announce itself, because both copies answer
plausibly.

`1af25e7` converged the two duplicates the ledger happened to record and swept
for no others. Resolve this one the same way -- one owner in `js/dungeon.js`,
`js/mklev.js` repointed, the alias removed -- and confirm an identical
development score, which is the only evidence a behavior-preserving move needs.

`js/hack.js endRunning()` carries the comment "gt.travelmap has no ported
counterpart, so its selection_free() is absent." That is false, and acting on
it would delete live code.

`grep -rn "travelmap" js/ scripts/` returns exactly two lines: that comment,
and `js/detect.js state.travelmap = null;`. The second sits inside a function
headed "C ref: hack.c nomul(0), including end_running(TRUE)'s state effects",
so it *is* a port of `hack.c`'s travelmap clear.

The defect underneath the comment is that `hack.c end_running()` has two
disagreeing ports. `js/hack.js endRunning()` does not clear `travelmap`; the
copy inside `js/detect.js` does. A reader who trusts the comment concludes the
`detect.js` line is unported scaffolding and removes it.

Resolve by deciding which function owns `end_running()`'s state effects --
`hack.c` names `js/hack.js` -- moving the clear there, having the `detect.js`
path call it, and correcting the comment. Confirm an identical development
score: whichever way the ownership falls, no scored session should observe a
difference today, because the two paths already agree on the value written.

Found by an audit of absence claims across `js/` comments on 6 August 2026.
That audit checked 53 such claims and found 14 false or stale, so this entry is
one instance of a class rather than an isolated slip.

Two placement leftovers found while closing the last sweep slice at `a448201`.

**`mon_allowflags()` is in the wrong file.** C owns it at `mon.c:2064`, so
`AGENTS.md` "Keep each source file's port in one place" puts it in `js/mon.js`;
the port has it at `js/monmove.js`. It carries a second copy of the
`can_tunnel` clearing that `m_move()` also performs, which is placement only
rather than a duplicate port -- C duplicates it too. Note that the `m_move()`
copy now has seven mutants killed by a dedicated test while this one has no
comparable coverage, so move it with a test rather than without.

**`monst.h:251 helpless()` is ported once and inlined three times.** The port
is `js/mhitm.js helpless()`. Three call sites reimplement its body inline and
cite the same C line rather than importing it: two in `js/steed.js` and one in
`js/dog.js`. The bodies agree today.

The second is the fourth duplicate-port finding of 6 August 2026, after
`isok()`, `will_weld()` and `depth()`. Unlike those it is an inlining rather
than a second definition, so a duplicate-export report would not list it; only
reading finds this shape.

Four follow-ups found while applying the correctness pass over
`a97c0a1..e9723ab`, none of them in its fourteen findings.

**`count_apes()` carries the identical defect the pass fixed three times over.**
Its comment cites the port's missing `AUTOPICKUP_EXCEPTION` statement as
evidence that the exception list is empty. `cfgfiles.c` has
`CNFL_N(AUTOPICKUP_EXCEPTION, 5)`, so C reads such a statement and the port
drops it. Adding a fourth row to `UNPORTED_CONFIG_STATEMENTS` closes it in
about three lines, and it is the same reasoning error: the port's own gap
offered as a fact about the game.

**A boolean written by an unhandled `OPTIONS=<name>:true` is stored as the
string `'true'`.** The options menu now refuses to display it, so the wrong
value cannot reach a screen through that path, but it stays wrong wherever else
it is read.

**`createCommandBindingModel()` does not skip `INTERNALCMD` rows** the way
`cmd.c bind_key()` does, so a binding to an internal command succeeds in the
port and fails in C.

**The port has no non-fatal config error.** `optfn_sortloot()`,
`optfn_versinfo()` and `optfn_msg_window()` all call `config_error_add()` and
let the game continue; the port throws. Matching C there is its own slice, and
it is the shape most likely to cost screens: C keeps playing where the port
stops.

notes.text: Three of the four residues are closed; only the non-fatal config error is left, and it is what the entry now waits on. count_apes() was fixed in 65d1bba, which added the AUTOPICKUP_EXCEPTION row to UNPORTED_CONFIG_STATEMENTS and the refusal inside count_apes(); e269420 added the menu-count test it had lacked. createCommandBindingModel() gained bind_key()'s INTERNALCMD skip in 6605941. The boolean stored as the string 'true' is unchanged. A sibling divergence found while reading bind_key() is also unchanged and is deliberate: a `bind` statement naming a command in no extcmdlist[] row still binds the key in this port, where C leaves it alone, and cmd.c count_bind_keys() compensates by looking the name up before comparing (js/cmd.js:1721-1727).

The non-fatal config error, this entry's fourth residue, is ported: optfn_sortloot(), optfn_versinfo() and optfn_msg_window() now reach cfgfiles.c config_error_add() instead of throwing, the errors are raw-printed through win/tty/wintty.c tty_raw_print() and dismissed at config_error_done()'s wait_synch(), and three fresh differentials match C on every random-number call and cursor. optfn_pickup_burden() and parsebindings()'s unknown-command error went the same way.

The entry stays open on its second residue, which no part of this slice touched: an unhandled compound option's value is still stored raw, so OPTIONS=<name>:true leaves the string 'true' in result.flags[name] (js/options.js applyOption()'s final else). No blockedOn is recorded because that residue waits on no single C symbol -- it is retired one optfn_ handler at a time, whichever option a reader of that flag needs.

The note at e269420 counted three of four residues closed while also reporting this one unchanged; the enumeration it gives names only two fixes plus a test.

The second residue -- an unhandled compound option's value stored raw -- now has
a number. A C recording of all 285 spellings of the three-suffix sweep in
scripts/config-error.test.mjs ('', ':' and ':zqxj' against each of the 95
non-pfx CompOpt rows) puts 45 of those rows in the residue: C writes 105

Correction to this entry's `is_launcher` line, and to the reasoning in the
commit that opened it.

That line was written from the working tree while the `twoweapon-command` slice
held it mid-edit, so it described the slice's uncommitted change as if it were
pre-existing state. At `5dd14ef`, before the slice landed, `js/worn.js:401` was
module-private `isLauncher`; `e4d15db` renamed and exported it as
`is_launcher` at :403. The line reads true at the current head only because the
slice made it true.

That inverts the attribution in the opening commit. It said a report correcting
the "unported" claim was itself wrong about which spellings exist. It was not:
the goal-selector's account -- both `is_launcher` ports module-private and
camelCase -- was correct for the tree as it then stood, and the orchestrator's
correction of it was the error. The slice worker caught this and said so.

The entry's substance is unaffected. `is_ammo` still has five live ports, one
per file in `js/obj.js`, `js/worn.js`, `js/startup_skills.js`, `js/invent.js`
and `js/u_init_inventory_attrs.js`, re-counted from the committed head rather

The transferable lesson is about method, not this area: while a worker holds
the working tree, verify a claim about repository state against a committed
ref -- `git show <sha>:<path>` -- because a plain grep reads a mutating tree
and cannot tell an in-flight edit from history.

scripts/mutate-sites.mjs reported js/exper.js:178 as a first-wave survivor during hero-combat slice 4, but `node --test scripts/mon-kill.test.mjs` fails on that exact mutant, verified twice by hand, and mon-kill.test.mjs is in the runner's own covering list for js/exper.js. A survivor the covering suite actually kills is a false survivor, which is the direction that wastes triage effort rather than the direction that hides defects, but it undermines the instrument either way.

The structural reason is that the mutator's site set is operators and literals, so it cannot express dropping a whole disjunct, which is the defect shape both passes kept finding. A false survivor on top of that makes the number harder still to read.

Closing condition: reproduce the disagreement on js/exper.js:178, find whether the fault is in the covering-file selection, the first-wave harness, or the report, and add a test that pins whichever it is.

notes.text:
Closed by the tests deferral burn-down. The disagreement does not reproduce; the instrument was right and the entry misidentified the mutant. js/exper.js:178 is unchanged since the entry was written (`git show 6fc50ef:js/exper.js` and the working tree hold the same `for (i = 0, tmp2 = 20; nk > tmp2 && tmp > 1; ++i) {`), and it carries three relational or logical mutants, not one. Rerunning all three at 1305c8d through a hand-written report and `node scripts/mutate-sites.mjs --from-report <path> --kind relational,logical,boolean` judged each separately: `nk > tmp2` -> `nk >= tmp2` at column 35 and `&&` -> `||` at column 42 were killed by scripts/mon-kill.test.mjs, which the run itself lists in the first wave for js/exper.js; `tmp > 1` -> `tmp >= 1` at column 49 survived. Applying each substitution by hand to js/exper.js and running `node --test scripts/mon-kill.test.mjs` agreed: 1 of 30 tests failed under the column-35 mutant and 0 of 30 under the column-49 one. The surviving mutant cannot be killed by any test. exper.c experience() (nethack-c/upstream/src/exper.c:157) enters the loop with tmp at least 1, `Math.trunc((1 + 1) / 2)` is 1, and i and nk are dead after the loop, so continuing at tmp === 1 changes neither tmp nor the returned value; simulating both conditions over tmp 1..3000 and nk 0..400, which covers the one-byte kill count svm.mvitals[].died supplies, found no differing pair. So the fault lies in none of the covering-file selection, the first wave, or the report: the entry named the mutant by line alone, and two of the three replace `>` with `>=`, so line and replacement together do not identify one. Closed with the assertion that pins the identity which separates them.

deferred.detail:
`js/do_wear.js armoroff()` ports only do_wear.c's no-delay branch at 1973-2005. The moment the delay computed at 1923 is non-zero it raises UnsupportedTakeOffError, before anything is drawn and before the piece leaves its slot.

C instead calls nomul(delay), sets gm.multi_reason to "disrobing", points ga.afternmv at the slot's <X>_off() and sets gn.nomovemsg to "You finish taking off your <what>." (do_wear.c:1930-1972), so the hero is helpless for that many turns and the item comes off at the end.

Reproduce it with a Samurai, who starts in splint mail (oc_delay 5):

  node scripts/diff-fresh.mjs --seed 7710101 --datetime 20310203040506 \
    --role Samurai --gender male --align lawful --name TakeOff \
    --options 'pettype:none,!acoustics,!autopickup,!legacy,!tutorial,!splash_screen' \
    --moves '.T.'

C prints nothing for the T, spends five turns and then prints the nomovemsg suit_simple_name() built, which for splint mail is "You finish taking off your mail."; the port stops on the T with the screen the preceding wait left. scripts/take-off-armor.test.mjs pins the stop and its position; the case is kept out of the passing matrix in scripts/run-take-off-armor.mjs because it does not match C.

notes.text:
The closing sentence names the wrong blocker. `nomul() has two owners and they disagree` was fixed by `daae919` ("Give hack.c end_running() and nomul() one port each"), an ancestor of this head; `js/detect.js defaultNomulZero()` is gone (`grep -rn defaultNomulZero js/ scripts/` returns 0), and `grep -rn 'function nomul' js/` returns exactly one line, `js/hack.js:501`. That deferral was left open by a bookkeeping omission and is closed alongside this note.

What actually blocks the delayed branch is narrower than the entry implies, and none of it is nomul():

- `ga.afternmv` has no port at all. `grep -rn afternmv js/` returns 6 hits, all comments in js/eat.js and js/do_wear.js. There is no field, no storage and no place that fires one when `multi` reaches zero. js/allmain.js already owns the negative-`multi` helpless path, so that is where the hook belongs, but it is unwritten.
- `gn.nomovemsg` has a field and readers but no consumer that prints it at the end of a wait; js/eat.js:944 writes it and done_eating() prints its own message inline. The same allmain.js firing point would own both, and eat.js's write should then route through it.
- `gm.multi_reason = \"disrobing\"` is a one-line write for fidelity; nomul() already clears the field and nothing reads it.
- Five of the seven `<X>_off()` bindings already exist in the no-delay switch. Only Gloves_off() and Boots_off() are missing.

An answered yn_function() prompt keeps its terminal row in C and loses it here whenever no message follows before the next flush_screen(1).

js/getline.js:307, inside tty_yn_function(), paints the prompt with show_topl() and then sets state._pending_message = ''. js/display.js:3327-3345 _buildScreenOutput() -- which flush_screen() calls, and which cmd.c parse() reaches through beginCommandParse() before every command key -- clears the whole grid and repaints row 0 from _pending_message alone. The physical prompt row therefore survives only until the next flush, while C's tty_clear_nhwindow(WIN_MESSAGE) is not called until after that key has been read.

A following pline() hides it, because rememberPendingMessage() refills _pending_message, which is why no recorded case had reached it. [abcd or ?*]". The same recipe with moves " .." passes, so the divergence needs the answered prompt.

The behavior scan's reconciliation reports 10 unreconciled stops where .agents/selection.md states the count is 0. The cause is structural, not a regression: the modeled half derives its supported set from key bindings and the ported-command list, so it cannot see an unported branch INSIDE a ported command. Four confirmed instances: seed0006's options menu, seed0361's wish tail, seed0367's garlic_breath(), seed0900's count prefix. The pickup-command goal added a fifth while it was open -- 'pickup' entered ADMITTED_COMMANDS in 8c64c2f while pickup() still refused inside it -- which resolved when the second slice landed. The effect on goal selection is real: a selector that ranks from the behavior table alone gets no row for these boundaries, and the 68-step seed0361 wish-tail candidate surfaced only because a selector ranked the recorded screens by hand. Close it by making the reconciliation model a command's supported branches rather than its admission, or, if that is too costly, by having the scan report the unreconciled set as a named category the selector is told to rank by hand, and by correcting .agents/selection.md, which asserts the count is 0.

notes.text: Closed. Both halves of the closing condition are met. deferred.detail: js/hack.js domove_fight_empty() refuses every force-fight by a hero wielding a pick or an axe, which is dig.c:173 dig_typ()'s own first test and no more. What remains is, for is_axe(uwep), refuse only closed_door(x, y) or IS_TREE(typ); for is_pick(uwep), refuse only closed_door(x, y) or (!IS_TREE(typ) && IS_OBSTRUCTED(typ) && (!level.flags.arboreal || IS_WALL(typ))). It is a slice rather than a small fix because it makes an axe hero's swing at a wall live, which needs its own recorded C differential. scripts/force-fight.test.mjs's PICK_AXE/AXE row currently pins the port's refusal at a VWALL; its comment now says so.
