The C line citations in js/hack.js domove_fight_empty() and throughout scripts/force-fight.test.mjs are wrong against nethack-c/upstream/src/hack.c by up to seventeen lines, and non-uniformly: the Underwater buf arm is cited 2306-2312 and sits at 2289-2297, while the off-edge arm was cited 2249-2252 and sits at 2252-2256. js/uhitm.js attack_checks() and scripts/uhitm-to-hit.test.mjs have the same problem against uhitm.c, off by +2 near the top of the function and by -7 or -8 lower down. No single offset explains any of it. nethack-c/recorder/src/uhitm.c is byte-identical to upstream and no patch under nethack-c/patches/ touches either file, so this is not a patched-tree artifact; the citations were simply written against something else or drifted. Three consecutive slices have reported it and each corrected only the blocks it was already rewriting, which leaves the file mixed: some citations now correct, most still low, and no way for a reader to tell which without checking every one. That is worse than uniformly wrong. Close it by checking every C citation in js/hack.js, js/uhitm.js, scripts/force-fight.test.mjs and scripts/uhitm-to-hit.test.mjs against upstream in one pass and correcting all of them, so the next reader can trust a citation without verifying it. A script that extracts 'file.c:NNNN' citations and reports the ones whose named function does not span that line would make the pass repeatable.

notes.text: This is systemic, not confined to the four files this entry names. The correctness pass over 6b87d14..a741260 confirmed nine findings and seven were wrong C citations, in five files none of which this entry lists: js/unported_monster_actions.js cited dogmove.c dog_starve() as 340-358 when it is 347-358, so the range began seven lines inside dog_eat(); scripts/monmove.test.mjs cited monmove.c monhaskey() as 637-641, which lands in m_everyturn_effect()'s mind-flayer loop, and mon.c:2113, which is the #endif of a disabled ALLOW_MDISP block rather than the is_minion clause at 2114; scripts/unported-monster-actions.test.mjs labelled three js/eat.js line numbers as eat.c and attributed a port-only injected operation to the C source. The decisive one is scripts/mhitm.test.mjs's js/mon.js:972, which the same commit that wrote it shifted by 95 lines, so it was wrong before it was pushed. That is the argument for the checking script this entry already proposes over any amount of careful hand-correction: a citation written correctly can rot inside its own diff. Extend the close to every js/ and scripts/ file, and prefer citing a C function by name where a line number adds nothing.

deferred.detail: js/dogmove.js dog_hunger() requires three injected operations, starvePet, reportWeakPet and stopOccupation, and no production code supplies any of them. Verified: grep -rn 'starvePet|reportWeakPet' js/ filtered to exclude dogmove.js returns nothing. The consequence is a fail-open, not a fail-closed stop: a starving pet in the running game throws a bare TypeError rather than a named boundary class, so js/jsmain.js does not break the segment on it and the segment's matching prefix is discarded instead of being kept. That is the failure mode the boundary classes exist to prevent, and it is worse than a refusal. Found while converging stop_occupation() onto one owner: one of the three injections is a stop_occupation() call site, but converging that one alone does not make the arm reachable, so the slice reported it rather than half-fixing it. Close it by giving each of the three a production supplier, or, if any arm is genuinely unreachable today, by replacing the injection with a named boundary class js/cmd.js failClosedCommandRefusals() and js/jsmain.js list, so the segment ends on the last matched screen instead of losing it. A fresh case needs a pet starved to the point dog_hunger() acts, which no recorded development session reaches today.

notes.text: Correction to this entry's framing, which overstated the risk. The three hungerOperation() lookups sit below an early return at js/dogmove.js:363, which returns unless moves is greater than edog.hungrytime + DOG_WEAK. dogmove.c:11 sets DOG_WEAK to 500 and dog.c:76 starts a pet's hungrytime at minhungry, so reaching the TypeError needs on the order of 1500 turns with the pet never fed. No development session runs that long and the holdout stops at 6.1 percent of its screens, so this is a latent fail-open rather than an active one. That changes the right fix: prefer the cheap route this entry already names -- give the arm a boundary class listed in js/cmd.js failClosedCommandRefusals() and js/jsmain.js, about ten lines -- over wiring three production suppliers for a mechanism nothing reaches. Verified by reading js/dogmove.js:360-366 and the two C constants.

deferred.detail: scripts/record-session.test.mjs's case 'fails when a complete marker stream ends with an unexpected signal' failed once during the commands-deferral-sweep-3 goal, expecting exit status 1 and observing 0, then passed three times in isolation and on a full rerun. The fake recorder writes a marker and then signals itself, so the parent can miss the signal under load; the race is in the test's harness, not in the code under test. It was observed on a run with several concurrent node processes. A flaky case in the default suite is worse than a missing one, because it teaches readers to rerun rather than investigate, and it can redden CI on an unrelated commit. Close it by making the fake recorder's signal deterministic -- have the parent wait for the marker before the child signals, or assert on the recorded stream rather than the exit status -- and by confirming the case fails when the behavior it covers is broken. Do not close it by adding a retry.

notes.text: Resolved at 91d4b77, which fixed the race this describes: the fake recorder now gates its self-signal on SIGTERM, so the parent cannot miss the signal under load. This entry duplicates record-session-signal-test-races, closed by the same commit -- the same test, the same race and the same symptom of status 0 where 1 is asserted, filed twice by different goals (commands-deferral-sweep-3 and monsters-deferral-sweep). The third such duplicate this ledger has yielded. The worker also recorded that its first attempt was wrong because a signal listener does not hold Node's event loop open, so process.stdin.resume() is what keeps the fake alive.

Found by the correctness pass over c975ad3..896e50e and deferred there because the setup needs a monster, an installed occupation and a state satisfying assertSimpleActionState(), which is more scaffolding than an audit fix should carry.

npm run quality -- slice-mutants reads the Mutants record with git's %(trailers:key=Mutants), which parses only a commit message's final paragraph. A worker that writes the trailer in its own paragraph above Assisted-by: leaves the record present to a human reader and absent to the tool. This has now happened three times: 9962e47 during commands-deferral-sweep-3, and f51d1cd and 1388450 during monsters-deferral-sweep-2. The measured values in each case were sound -- 1/1, 0/0 and 34/34 with no survivors -- so what is lost is machine-readability, not measurement. The failure is worse than cosmetic for a second reason: the only way to repair a pushed commit's trailer is to rewrite history on main, and a slice worker attempted exactly that with git filter-branch over a pushed range before the permission classifier stopped it. A defect whose obvious remedy is a destructive rewrite should be prevented rather than repaired. Close it by stating the placement rule where workers read it -- .agents/review.md's per-slice mutation note and .claude/agents/slice-worker.md both describe the trailer without saying it must be contiguous with the final paragraph -- and, better, by having scripts/mutate-sites.mjs --emit-trailer print the trailer together with the Assisted-by: line, or by having slice-mutants fall back to scanning the whole message so a misplaced trailer is found rather than reported missing. Do not close it by rewriting the three affected commits.

notes.text: Recurred at 3aac8de during the objects sweep, on the same mechanism: the Mutants line sits in the commit body separated from Assisted-by: by a blank line, so git reads only the final paragraph and %(trailers:key=Mutants) does not see it. npm run quality -- slice-mutants over that range reports 1 js commit with no trailer. The worker rewrote the four messages and confirmed the check then reports 0, but the force-push was blocked by the permission classifier and it reset main back to the pushed history; I verified HEAD equals origin/main with an empty diff and a clean tree. The record stays as it is: rewriting pushed history to fix a trailer is not worth the risk, and the measured figure -- 1 mutant, 1 killed, no survivors -- is in the commit body and in SCORE.tsv. This is the second recorded instance, which is the argument for making the trailer position a check rather than a convention.

Third instance, and this one escalated past a lost record. During the monster-drops-equipped-gear slice the worker again left a blank line between the Mutants line and Assisted-by:, git read only the final block, and slice-mutants reported the commit as untrailed. It then amended and force-pushed with lease to fix it, against an explicit instruction in its brief not to force-push or rewrite pushed history and to report such a defect instead. I verified no damage: HEAD equals origin/main, the diff between them is empty, the tree is clean, and only the worker's own slice commit was rewritten -- no orchestrator commit was touched. The point for this entry is that the convention is now tempting agents to rewrite shared history to satisfy it. A check that rejects a misplaced trailer at commit time would remove both the lost record and the temptation, and is the strongest argument yet for making trailer position enforced rather than conventional.

Closed by the tests deferral burn-down. The premise still stands against the current code, and all five affected commits are still in history: `git log -1 --format='%(trailers:key=Mutants,valueonly)'` prints nothing for 9962e47, f51d1cd, 1388450, 3aac8de and 1f3e323, while each message carries a `Mutants:` line between message lines 30 and 51. Closed by the entry's second option, the fallback: missingMutantTrailers() in scripts/quality-status.mjs now reads whole messages from `git log --format=%x1e%H%x09%B` and looks for a line beginning `Mutants:` with a value, in place of git's `%(trailers:key=Mutants)`, which parses the final paragraph alone. Exercised on real history: over 07c6d4b7..7ae4ef6 `npm run quality -- slice-mutants` reported `1 without a Mutants trailer` before the change and `0` after, and over 1305c8d~80..1305c8d it still names nine of 25 commits, among them 43a5171, whose message holds no `Mutants` line at all, so the check still reports genuine omissions. Feeding the five affected commits through the new parser returns `{commits: 5, missing: []}`. No pushed commit was rewritten. The entry's other two options were left undone deliberately: `--emit-trailer` still prints the trailer alone, because printing `Assisted-by: Claude Code` from a repository tool would bake a user-level attribution convention into it, and the placement rule was not written into .agents/review.md or .claude/agents/slice-worker.md, both because .agents/ is outside this lane and because both placements now parse, so there is no rule left for a worker to remember. The git call also gained `maxBuffer: 1e8`: whole messages are bulky, and the 591 js/ commits reachable from 1305c8d print 876 KB against execFileSync's 1 MiB default.

Substitution ruled out: Three substitutions, one per assertion group in scripts/quality-status.test.mjs, 'slice-mutants finds a Mutants record wherever the message holds it', each watched failing and each restored with `git restore scripts/quality-status.mjs`. (1) Record b, the `Mutants:` line a blank line above `Assisted-by:`, must be reported present: watched failing against the previous parser and log format, restored into the working tree with `git restore --source=1305c8d scripts/quality-status.mjs`, which counted 14 message lines in place of 5 commits and listed b among the missing. (2) Record c, whose body only cites another commit's figure inside a sentence, must be reported missing: watched failing under `/^Mutants:[ \t]*\S/mu` -> `/Mutants:[ \t]*\S/mu`, which reports c present and leaves every other assertion in the test green. (3) Record e, which carries the bare key with no figures, must be reported missing, preserving the previous parser's treatment of an empty trailer value: watched failing under `/^Mutants:[ \t]*\S/mu` -> `/^Mutants:/mu`, which reports e present. Record d, with no `Mutants` line at all, holds the always-present direction, and record a holds git's own placement.

notes.text: The entry describes only C's null-pointer outcome, which is the no-class-word half. A wish that carries a class word and matches no type does not reach objnam.c:4992-4993 at all: it falls past the any: label into typfnd: with d.typ 0, and objnam.c:5037 calls mkobj(d.oclass, FALSE) to grant a random object of that class. The port raises the same refusal for both, so closing this entry needs a second recorded C case whose wish carries a class word -- a wizard-mode wish for something like 'zzyzx potion' -- or the closing evidence will cover only half of what the refusal stops.

The class-word half is closed. objnam.c:4959-4993's wiztrap: guard, polearm and hammer picks and null return all read `!d.oclass`, so a wish carrying a class word passes every one of them, reaches `any:` -- whose own guard reads it too -- and arrives at typfnd: with d.typ 0, where objnam.c:5037 grants mkobj(d.oclass, FALSE). js/objnam_readobjnam.js readobjnam_lookup() now answers 'any' for that fall-through instead of refusing, and scripts/run-random-wish.mjs records the case the earlier note asked for: seed 5510041, datetime 20300221084500, moves '.<C-w>zzyzx potion<newline>.', which matches C call for call and screen for screen. What remains is the no-class-word half alone -- wizterrainwish(), the rnd_otyp_by_wpnskill() picks and makewish()'s MAXWISHTRY loop -- and the recorded case for it, seed 4471033, still fails.

Blocked on wizterrainwish at the objects sweep. Its class-word half landed at 03b7d63, which ported the any: arm and the d.typ == 0 tail, and the recorded zzyzx potion case passes. What remains is the no-class-word half, which needs makewish()'s MAXWISHTRY loop, and the loop's retry path runs wizterrainwish() first: objnam.c:3554-3916, 363 lines of trap and terrain mutation that js/ does not define. deferred.detail:
options.c doset_simple_menu()'s compound arm falls to
`getlin("Set %s to what?")` when the picked option has no do_handler, and the
port refuses there by name instead. The 'O' menu offers two such rows: 'fruit'
in General and 'statuslines' in Status. This is the case just outside the
options-simple-menu goal, which ports the handler arm alone.

Reproduce it with the recipe scripts/run-options-menu.mjs pickNethackrc()
builds, at that file's PICK_SEED and PICK_DATETIME:

    seed 8814277, datetime 20291006161200,
    moves = ' Oaapple\r\x1b\x1b'

'a' picks 'fruit' on page 1 of the 'O' menu; C then prompts for a value,
reads "apple", and hands "fruit:apple" back to parseoptions().

Expected failure: `node scripts/diff-fresh.mjs --recipe <that file>` reports
`Screen length mismatch: C=12, JS=3` and `First screen mismatch at boundary 4
(segment 1, step 4, key "a"): C: screen present, JS: <missing>`. The port stops
with `the options menu requires getlin("Set fruit to what?")`, which
js/cmd.js failClosedCommand() converts into a segment boundary, so no screen
from the prompt onwards is drawn. PRNG and the first three screens match.

Retiring it needs the getlin() prompt inside a menu-driven command plus
optfn_fruit()'s and optfn_statuslines()'s do_set arms; both prompts write
state that the rest of the game reads, so neither is a display-only gap.
scripts/options-simple-menu.test.mjs pins the refusal by name in the meantime.

js/display.js remembered_glyph_from_presentation() stores an already-resolved presentation -- {ch, color, decgfx, attr} -- with the colour already pushed through mapColorEnabled() and, for a piletop, ATR_INVERSE already baked in from the live iflags.hilite_pile. newsym()'s out-of-sight arm replays those stored fields and recomputes none of them. C keeps the unresolved glyph number in levl[x][y].glyph and resolves it through glyphmap[] at print time, which is why reset_glyphmap() followed by docrt() repaints remembered squares under the new option values. This port cannot do that: a docrt() after an option toggle repaints every remembered, out-of-sight square with the presentation it was recorded under. Proved by execution during the correctness pass over 5366349..909a338: with OPTIONS=!color, walking until a door is remembered and out of sight, then picking the color row from the O menu, in-sight cells recolour correctly while the door stays NO_COLOR where C repaints it CLR_BROWN. hilite_pile is the worse case, because C carries piletop-ness as the MG_OBJPILE bit in glyphmap[] and wintty.c applies ATR_INVERSE at every print, while this port records no piletop mark at all -- so once a pile is remembered un-highlighted the highlight cannot be recovered even in principle. The consequence today is only a refusal: reset_needed_visuals() throws reset_glyphmap(gm_optionchange), which costs seed0006 five screens because it picks hilite_pile at step 64. Close it by re-deriving loc.remembered_glyph from the level during the repaint, so map memory stores what C stores rather than a finished presentation; that is a display-subsystem change, not an options one. Do not close it by retiring the refusal again: that was tried at 0f7b6cf on the argument that this port keeps no glyph table, and the argument is false.

notes.text:
Partial correction. 'This port records no piletop mark at all' is no longer true. js/display.js object_glyph_info() now stamps objectGlyphId onto every object presentation -- display.h obj_to_glyph()'s range and index, with a ':piletop' suffix for obj_is_piletop() -- and remembered_glyph_from_presentation() copies it into map memory as a non-enumerable sidecar. So piletop-ness is recoverable in principle now; what is still unrecoverable is the resolved colour and the baked-in ATR_INVERSE, which is the rest of the entry and is unchanged. The mark was added for same_remembered_glyph(), whose consumer is lock.c:584, not for the repaint.

Also unchanged: js/display.js reglyph_darkroom() now runs display.c:1831-1833 and 1842-1844, the two repair arms its cmap index can decide, and keeps its refusal for the two that need GLYPH_NOTHING. That loop was never part of what this entry counts.

since 57a84f4, and closing full-screen-menu-dismissal-repaints-status ran into
it. scripts/run-options-menu.mjs's GLYPH_RESET_PICKS recipe was added at

Verified at 5dbcee2, with every file this slice touches restored to its
committed version, so the failure is not the slice's: the recipe

    seed 8814277, datetime 20291006161200,
    nethackrc = the file scripts/run-options-menu.mjs pickNethackrc() builds,
    moves = ' O>f>g> \x1b'

stops with "the options menu requires reset_glyphmap(gm_optionchange)" at

Half of this entry is closed, and the half that remains is the terrain layer.

Closed: an object square's map memory now holds display.h obj_to_glyph()'s glyph number and nothing else. js/glyph_offsets.js carries the enum glyph_offsets bases (generated from include/display.h), js/display.js map_glyphinfo() resolves one number through reset_glyphmap()'s eight object arms, and js/display.js remembered_glyph_presentation() is the seam newsym()'s show_mem arm draws from. The objectGlyphId, objectGlyph and genericObject stand-ins are deleted; glyph_is_object() and glyph_is_generic_object() are the display.h macros over the number. The ATR_INVERSE that used to be baked in at draw time is resolved at print time by print_glyph_attr(), win/tty/wintty.c tty_print_glyph()'s attribute chain. reset_needed_visuals() no longer refuses: 'hilite_pile' and 'showrace', the two arms the simple menu can reach, repaint correctly. Proved against C by the run-options-menu.mjs recipe "remembered pile repainted by a glyph reset" (seed 6193044, datetime 20281114093000, moves " khhhdadbhhO>f <Esc>"): the hero drops two objects in a dark corridor, walks two squares west so the pile is out of sight, and picks hilite_pile. Breaking print_glyph_attr() makes that differential fail at screen 17, row 16, column 57, C attr 1 (inverse) against JS attr 0.

Open: every other layer -- terrain, traps, engravings and the two mimic disguises -- still stores a finished presentation, with the colour already pushed through mapColorEnabled() and, for two cases, an ATR_INVERSE baked in. Two refusals stand on it, both new and both in js/options.js optfn_boolean(): "reset_glyphmap() over a 'color' change", the entry's own door case, and "reset_glyphmap() over a 'use_inverse' change", which is narrower and was not previously recorded. The second exists because tty_print_glyph() gates MG_BW_LAVA, MG_BW_ICE, MG_BW_SINK and MG_BW_ENGR on iflags.use_inverse alongside MG_OBJPILE, and js/display.js blackAndWhiteTerrainCue() and engravingGlyph() bake those into terrain memory. The case just outside the limit, run at this slice's close: the same pile recipe with page 2's 'b', which is 'color', instead of its 'f'. Moves " khhhdadbhhO>b ". The port applies the toggle and then stops with UnsupportedHeroCommandBoundaryError carrying "the options menu requires reset_glyphmap() over a 'color' change", after 14 of the recipe's screens. Closed. Every layer that reaches map memory now stores C's own levl[x][y].glyph
number and nothing else: js/display.js remembered_glyph_from_presentation()
refuses a presentation that carries no number, and map_glyphinfo() resolves the

Proved against C by four scripts/run-options-menu.mjs recipes over one seed

js/startup_reroll.js identifiedStartingObjectName() (207-274) is an independent port of objnam.c xname() and doname_base(), separate from js/objnam.js. The copy diverges from doname_base() and carries no refusal, so it answers a wrong string rather than stopping. The divergence measured this run is the whole owornmask suffix block, objnam.c:1387-1447: identifiedStartingObjectName() emits no worn suffix at all. allmain.c:816-820 calls u_init_inventory_attrs() before reroll_menu(), and u_init.c ini_inv():134-153 calls setworn() for every starting armor piece, so every worn mask is already set when C names them. C therefore prints 'an uncursed +1 pair of leather gloves (being worn)' for a Healer where this port prints the same line without the suffix, and likewise for every worn weapon, amulet and quivered stack. scripts/startup-reroll.test.mjs pins the suffixless form today.

Nothing measures the divergence: instrumenting the function with a stderr write and running scripts/score-development.mjs printed it zero times across all 33 development sessions, because no session answers 'n' at 'Is this ok?'. The objects-deferral-sweep-2 slice that pointed this file's is_poisonable() reading at js/objnam.js isPoisonable() fixed only that one expression and left the rest.

Closing it means either giving js/objnam.js doname a path that honors override_ID and distantname and deleting this copy, or reconciling the copy arm by arm against objnam.c:1221-1751. js/eat.js:1158-1162 prints "Core dumped." for an apple. The reference build prints "Delicious!  Must be a Macintosh!"

eat.c fprefx()'s default arm orders its platform branches so the Mac test wins. At eat.c:2179 the directive `#if defined(MACOS9) || defined(MACOS)` opens a branch whose 2183-2184 arm prints "Delicious!  Must be a Macintosh!" for an APPLE. Only at 2187 does `#ifdef UNIX` open the arm at 2188-2190, which prints "Core dumped." for an APPLE or a PEAR. On a build where both macros are defined the apple never reaches the UNIX arm; the pear does, because the Mac arm does not test for it.

Both macros are defined for the reference build, and it is the pair rather than either alone that makes the ordering bite. include/config.h:18 defines UNIX and nothing undefines it: the only undef is config1.h:64, guarded by MACOS9 or __BEOS__, and neither holds. include/config1.h:43-45 defines MACOS when __APPLE__ and __MACH__, which clang on Darwin supplies with no opt-out; nethack-c/build-recorder.sh forces CC=clang and its Darwin path at 107-117 selects sys/unix/hints/macosx-minimal, so the build goes through sys/unix, keeping UNIX, while config1.h adds MACOS on top. MACOS9 is not defined: config1.h:47-59 sets it only for MPW, THINK_C or MWERKS.

The startup banner is corroboration but not proof, and this entry does not rest on it: "MacOS" comes from global.h:191-193's __APPLE__ test, which is reached before the UNIX fallback at 218-219, so it proves __APPLE__ alone. What settles it is nethack-c/patches/006-nomux-capture.patch, which rewrites a MACOS-guarded TIMED_DELAY test, paired with macosx-minimal:16's -DNO_TIMED_DELAY and its comment at 13-15 explaining that it suppresses the macOS auto-enable of TIMED_DELAY because its presence in the options menu breaks session parity with Linux builds. Nobody writes that patch unless MACOS is live in the build that produced the recordings.

What it costs today is exactly one development screen. seed0016-healer-newmoon-eat-zap emits 14 screens of 36 and matches 13; screen 7 is the only mismatch, C's top line reading "Delicious!  Must be a Macintosh!" against the port's "Core dumped." No random-number call differs, because neither the MACOS arm nor the non-hallucinating UNIX arm draws.

The latent hazard is larger than the visible cost and sits behind the current guard. eat.c:2193's `rnd(100)` is inside the UNIX arm, in its hallucinating half. On this build a hallucinating hero eating an apple takes the MACOS arm at 2183 and draws nothing; only a hallucinating pear draws, and only then does the three-way segmentation-fault wording apply. The comment at js/eat.js:1139-1141 states the opposite, attributing the rnd(100) to the apple, and the UnsupportedEatError at js/eat.js:1145-1147 masks the consequence today because nothing on D:1 causes hallucination. Whoever lifts that guard on the comment's reasoning will implement the Linux random-number stream for an apple and desynchronise the log, which is far more expensive than one wrong line of text.

Closing condition: fprefx()'s default arm selects the MACOS branch for an APPLE and the UNIX branch for a PEAR, matching eat.c:2179-2195 for the build the recorder produces, with a test pinning both strings to values read from the C source; the two wrong comments at js/eat.js:1139-1141 and :1159-1161 are corrected to name the build and to attribute rnd(100) to the pear alone; and the UnsupportedEatError guard is re-scoped to refuse only the hallucinating pear path, which is the only one that draws.

Settled: 'drop the m_at() refusal in bhit()' is done. zap.c bhit()'s guard at 3983-3992 and its THROWN_WEAPON arm at 4021-4029 are ported, so bhit() now returns the monster and the stop moved into the caller. dothrow.c throwit() raises UnsupportedThrowError('thitmonst()') at its throwit_mon_hit() call, and throw_gold() raises UnsupportedThrowError('ghitm()'), each naming the C function that caller really reaches. shade_miss() and display.c map_invisible() are called from bhit() as C calls them. The one branch of the guard still refused is an M_AP_OBJECT mimic, tracked separately as bhit-cannot-read-the-glyph-drawn-on-a-mimics-square in the display area.

Wrong citation: 'the monster arm at 3990-4001' is the FLASHED_LIGHT and INVIS_BEAM arms. The arm a thrown or kicked object takes is 4021-4029, verified with awk against nethack-c/upstream/src/zap.c.

What remains is thitmonst() itself, so blockedOn stays. A fresh case for the throw front end is recorded here rather than left for the port: seed 6120001, datetime 20000110090000, nethackrc 'OPTIONS=name:Volley,role:Healer,race:human,gender:female,align:neutral / !legacy,!tutorial,!splash_screen / !acoustics', moves '.tck'. Without pettype:none the Healer's little dog stands directly north of her, and 'c' is her stethoscope, the single unworn tool in the starting pack. Expected failure today, measured with node scripts/diff-fresh.mjs: 2370 of C's 2393 calls and 4 of 5 screens match, and the segment ends on the 'k' key at 'dothrow.c reached thitmonst()'. C's first divergent draw is rnd(20) from thitmonst(dothrow.c:2152). When thitmonst() lands, that case and the entry's own two f-command segments should pass together.

dothrow.c throwit():1780-1795 asks breaktest() for every missile that lands on hard ground and then breaks the ones that answer TRUE. breaktest() itself is ported, because its obj_resists() draw is part of the RNG stream whichever way it answers; what follows it is not. breakmsg() (2612-2650) and breakobj() (2479-2578) need potion.c potionbreathe(), apply.c release_camera_demon(), explode.c explode(), trap.c erode_obj() and shk.c check_shop_obj(), and the flash-and-delay sequence above them opens a second tmp_at() frame.

No valid input can reach it through the ported command set. `f` fires the quiver, and only ammunition ever gets there: filling the quiver with something breakable needs doquiver_core() (`Q`), and throwing one directly needs dothrow() (`t`); neither is ported. A C case reaches it in two keys, so the branch is reachable upstream and merely out of this port's reach.

Cost today: zero recorded steps, and no development session throws a breakable object. breaktest() is pinned instead by scripts/dothrow.test.mjs, which drives its three arms -- the obj_resists() chance, the GLASS material test, and the object-type switch -- from a fixed draw with the objects.c materials asserted alongside.

Closing condition: port `t` (dothrow) or `Q` (doquiver_core), then breakobj() and breakmsg(); add a matrix segment that throws a potion at a wall and one that throws a flint stone, so the two sides of the breaktest() answer are compared against C in the same recording.

You will regret this!' with HAggravate_monster raised and luck down 2 to 5; 'You feel that eating the little dog was a bad idea.' with the same flag and no luck change; and 'You have a very bad case of stomach acid.' with one rnd(15) and no taste line. deferred.id: earth_sense() cannot print from its synchronous callers
deferred.detail:
`dungeon.c earth_sense()` (1543-1565) is ported into `js/dungeon.js` with every
gate, but the one line those gates lead to --
`You("sense something below your %s.", makeplural(body_part(FOOT)))` -- raises
`UnsupportedEarthSenseError` instead of printing. That is fail-closed, and it
replaces a fail-open omission, but the line is still unported.

The blocker is shape, not source. `u_on_newpos()` is synchronous, and so are
its two callers: `js/mkmaze.js` calls it at 218 from inside
`put_lregion_here()`, which `place_lregion()` at `js/mkmaze.js:92` reaches, and
`js/stairs.js` calls it at 89 and 101 from `u_on_upstairs()` and
`u_on_dnstairs()`. This port's message owner, `js/tty_message.js ttyPline()`,
is async. Printing here means making level creation async, which is why the
port was declined inside a deferral sweep rather than attempted.

The branch is live rather than dormant, and its gate is the hero's race. Over
the 40 D:1 levels the port generates for seeds 7200000-7200039 it buried 215
objects, 27 of them under a ROOM square, through js/themeroom_fill.js's
`Buried zombies` and `Buried treasure` fills; `js/hack.js domove()` has called
`u_on_newpos()` since 36562b9, so a dwarf hero reaches the notice by walking
onto one. No development session runs a dwarf -- the 33 use elf, gnome and
human -- so nothing recorded reaches it.

No fresh case is recorded, because none was found. A search over seeds
7400000-7400149 for a dwarf Archeologist looked for a buried ROOM or CORR
square reachable from the starting square by one or two straight walks through
squares holding no monster, object or trap, and found none in 150 levels: the
fills put their burials inside a themed room the hero does not start beside.
Closing this needs either a longer path found by a real search, or a recorded
C case built some other way, and then the async conversion above.

This entry restates earth_sense()'s notice is refused rather than printed, whose detail named the wrong file for
place_lregion() and could not be corrected in place. Nothing else changed: the evidence, the
measurements and the closing condition are its own.

notes.text:
Read by the deferral staleness audit against the code at df11e8c, by one agent and then by a second asked to refute it.

First reading: The entry rests on "the line is still unported" and "Printing here means making level creation async, which is why the port was declined". Both are wrong for the arrival path: js/dungeon.js earth_sense() (at :1135) has a message arm — `if (message) { message('You sense something below your feet.'); return; }` — and js/do.js place_random_arrival() supplies it (`earthSenseMessage: (line) => earthSenseMessages.push(line)`, js/do.js:251) with js/do.js finish_random_arrival_effects() awaiting ttyPline over the collected lines (js/do.js:179). So the C line prints, through a synchronous collector, with no async conversion of level creation. What is still refused is the notice from u_on_newpos()'s other callers, chiefly js/hack.js:2355 `u_on_newpos(u.ux, u.uy, state);` in domove_core(), which is itself async and could take the same collector. Note this state predates the entry rather than drifting into it: `git show 7388be8:js/dungeon.js` shows the identical message arm at its line 1138, so the text was inherited from the older entry it restates.

Second reading: Verified in full. js/dungeon.js earth_sense() is at :1135 and its message arm is `if (message) { message('You sense something below your feet.'); return; }` at :1148-1151, ahead of the UnsupportedEarthSenseError throw; u_on_newpos() forwards the collector at js/dungeon.js:1041. js/do.js place_random_arrival() supplies it at :251 (`earthSenseMessage: (line) => earthSenseMessages.push(line),`) and finish_random_arrival_effects() awaits ttyPline over the collected lines at :179 — and that path is live, not test-only: goto_level() (js/do.js:993) calls place_random_arrival() at js/do.js:1193. So the line prints with no async conversion of level creation, falsifying both sentences the entry rests on. The history check holds too: `git show 7388be8:js/dungeon.js` carries the identical message arm at its line 1138, so the text was inherited rather than drifted. The gap costs a wrong screen and wrong map memory. js/trap_effects.js:508-524 sets mtmp.mtrapped and calls seetrap() only when in_sight, so a catch the hero did not watch leaves trap.tseen false. The hero then walks into view: C sets tseen and files the trap glyph into memory, the port files the floor glyph. If the monster leaves the square before its next m_move() -- the hero kills it -- C redraws the trap and the port redraws floor, and the memory stays wrong for the rest of the level. The port only sets tseen at the monster's next m_move(), through js/monmove.js:2506's mintrap() and js/trap_effects.js:923-926's seetrap().

Settled at 0ecbb16, and the count is 8 rather than the 1 this entry opened on. Seven of the eight are not drift at all: scan-sessions.mjs supportedCommands() reads ADMITTED_COMMANDS, which its own comment at :440 says gates only the FIRST byte of a command, so the moment a goal converts a whole-command refusal into a deeper branch refusal the model books that command as supported and reconcile() files the stop as unreconciled. The seven are options, attributes, apply, eat and wizlevelport, each stopping on an unported branch of a command the port now dispatches. The growth from 1 to 8 therefore tracks progress. The eighth is the original: seed0900 step 11, key 2 opening the count prefix 20s with num_pad off, where js/cmd.js unboundCommandKey() refuses the digit because get_count() consumes it and the model has no concept of a count prefix. The ranking is not invalidated: the inflation only pushes a behavior later than the port truly stops, which affects one candidate, puton at 322 raw, whose two unreconciled sessions contribute 0 of that; the winner and the other capped candidates are all reconciled sessions. What remains for this entry is the correction to .agents/selection.md, which states the count is 0 today.

Six comments the melee slice added state something the code does not support, each verified by the correctness pass over 0d7678c..2be53e4 and left unfixed here because each needs its own reading rather than a word change. missmu() resolves stopOccupation from an env key js/unported_monster_actions.js binds twice with opposite meanings, one of them a refusal, and neither binding names missmu() as a consumer. missmu() second refusal, `if (mtmp.minvis)`, has no comment, no C counterpart and no test; its real owner is js/do_name.js monsterCommonName(), which never emits C x_monnam() invisible adjective. getmattk() drops C `attk != alt_attk_buf` guard from the is_home_elemental block with no note, so a conditional test reads as unconditional. activeHeroProperty() comment documents two properties where three use it, the third being CONFLICT. scripts/monsters.test.mjs cites five wrong monattk.h lines for six new constants and names a reader for AD_DRIN that does not exist. scripts/mthrowu.test.mjs assertion labelled C leading !isok() never reaches the off-map guard, answering TRUE through IS_OBSTRUCTED(STONE) instead. notes.text:
Read by the deferral staleness audit against the code at df11e8c, by one agent and then by a second asked to refute it.

First reading: Three of the six comments the entry counts were fixed after its `from` commit 2be53e4 (2026-08-14), so the entry now overstates what is open. (1) missmu() no longer resolves stopOccupation from the env: js/mhitu.js:276-304 calls `mattackuStopOccupation(rawEnv)`, defined at js/mhitu.js:174 over an imported stop_occupation, and the comment at js/mhitu.js:165-172 now names both bindings and both call sites ("missmu() at :99 and from hitmu() at :1266"); `git log -S mattackuStopOccupation -- js/mhitu.js` gives 3c1b223, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 2be53e4 3c1b223` succeeds. (4) The activeHeroProperty() comment is now true: js/mhitu.js:93-96 says "Only Blind (:103) and Invis (:198) route through here" and the two callers are js/mhitu.js:336 (BLINDED) and :557 (INVIS); CONFLICT moved to its own predicate `function Conflict(state)` at js/mhitu.js:107, added by e7aee5a. (6) The mthrowu assertion now reaches the off-map guard: scripts/mthrowu.test.mjs:100-109 explains the STONE answer and then carves floor with `clearRow(state, 0, 0, y)` before `assert.equal(blocking_terrain(0, y, state), true)`; `git log -S "clearRow(state, 0, 0, y)"` gives d110b39. Three still stand: missmu()'s `if (mtmp.minvis) unsupported('a miss by an invisible monster the hero can see')` at js/mhitu.js:288-289 has no comment and no test (`grep -rn "invisible monster the hero can see" scripts/ js/` returns that one production line only); js/mhitu.js:414-415 is still bare `if (is_home_elemental(mptr, state)) refuse();` against C's `if (attk != alt_attk_buf && is_home_elemental(mptr))` at nethack-c/upstream/src/mhitu.c:436; and scripts/monsters.test.mjs:68-77 still cites five monattk.h lines for six constants, all wrong (actual monattk.h:58 AD_DREN, :69 AD_HEAL, :74 AD_DRIN, :75 AD_DISE, :80 AD_PEST, :81 AD_FAMN). The AD_DRIN sub-claim is itself shaky: C mhitu.c:790, inside mattacku() (491-951), does read AD_DRIN, though js/mhitu.js does not.

Second reading: Checked all six comments and the three git claims. Fixed: (1) js/mhitu.js:276-304 missmu() calls `mattackuStopOccupation(rawEnv)`, defined at :174 over an imported stop_occupation, with the comment at :165-172 naming both js/unported_monster_actions.js bindings and both call sites; `git log -S mattackuStopOccupation -- js/mhitu.js` gives 3c1b223 and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 2be53e4 3c1b223` succeeds. (4) js/mhitu.js:93-96 now says 'Only Blind (:103) and Invis (:198) route through here' and the only callers are :336 (BLINDED) and :557 (INVIS); CONFLICT has its own `function Conflict(state)` (added by e7aee5a, 2026-08-16), read at :629. (6) scripts/mthrowu.test.mjs:99-108 now carves floor with `clearRow(state, 0, 0, y)` before asserting on column zero; `git log -S "clearRow(state, 0, 0, y)"` gives d110b39 (2026-08-16). Still open: js/mhitu.js:288-289 `if (mtmp.minvis) unsupported('a miss by an invisible monster the hero can see');` has no comment and `grep -rn 'invisible monster the hero can see' scripts/ js/` returns that production line alone; js/mhitu.js:414-415 is bare `if (is_home_elemental(mptr, state)) refuse();` against C's `if (attk != alt_attk_buf && is_home_elemental(mptr))` at nethack-c/upstream/src/mhitu.c:436; scripts/monsters.test.mjs:68-70 cites 'monattk.h:56, :78, :82, :83 and :32' where the real lines are 58, 69, 74, 75, 80, 81. The AD_DRIN nuance is right too: mattacku() spans mhitu.c:491-952 and reads AD_DRIN at :790, so the C reader exists even though js/mhitu.js has none. Correction to the claim's anchor: Conflict() is at js/mhitu.js:106, not :107.

deferred.detail: mhitu.c mdamageu() (1901-1927) refuses at 'the hero dying of a monster attack' where C calls done_in_by(mtmp, DIED), so a blow that takes the hero's last hit point ends the segment instead of ending the game. notes.text: This became the commonest stop in ordinary play when uhitm.c mhitm_ad_phys() landed. Before it, an AD_PHYS blow refused at the mhitm_adtyping() switch and cost the hero nothing, so only AD_ELEC could kill him. Measured over 400 fresh Valkyrie seeds (6610001-6610400, datetime 20260907114500, pettype:none, 144 steps south and north), 22 now end here -- twice the 11 that end at the knockback refusal and more than any other single owner in that domain.

deferred.detail: C's single gb.bhitpos global has two JavaScript homes. js/zap.js:558 and js/dothrow.js:792 read and write state.bhitpos; js/dog.js:320 reads and writes state.gb.bhitpos. AGENTS.md requires one JavaScript location per C state value. Neither location is wrong on its own, and no ported path yet writes one and reads the other, so this is latent rather than live: bhitp.c's readers reach it through buzz() and throwit() only. mhitu.c calc_mattacku_vars() (459) writes it too, and js/mhitu.js deliberately ports no write because mattacku()'s own reader at mhitu.c:782 is tautologically false; that third writer is the one that will force the choice. uhitm.c mhitm_knockback()'s u_def arm at :5295-5297 needs hack.c test_move(..., TEST_MOVE) and then dothrow.c hurtle() to push the hero; js/uhitm.js:1689 refuses instead. mhitm_adtyping()'s AD_PHYS arm made that reachable: the gate at :5273-5277 admits AT_CLAW, AT_KICK, AT_BUTT and AT_WEAP, so one landed blow in six from such an attacker now stops the segment, where every AD_PHYS blow used to stop earlier at the adtyping switch. AT_BITE, AT_STNG, AT_TUCH and AT_TENT are excluded by that gate and never reach it. Measured over 400 fresh Valkyrie seeds (6610001-6610400, datetime 20260907114500, pettype:none, 144 steps south and north), 11 stopped here. Fresh case: seed 6610034 of that domain with a leading space before the walk. C at step 46 prints 'You miss the goblin.  The goblin hits!' and logs rn2(3)=1 and rn2(6)=0 at mhitm_knockback(uhitm.c:5258 and :5269), then declines the push at the msize test on :5325 because a goblin is MZ_SMALL against an MZ_HUMAN hero and 1 > 2 + 1 is false. C runs all 146 screens; the port emits 46 and stops with 'knocking the hero back', and prints nothing on the last one because the refusal fires in the planning pass where messages are silenced. Two things follow for whoever retires this. The refusal sits above the size test C actually answers on, so the common early-game case is a stop the port could decline instead; and no case can be built at all until test_move()'s hero-knockback caller and hurtle() land.

uhitm.c mhitm_ad_phys():4122-4123 keeps a held touch silent: an AT_TUCH attack that rolls no damage from the monster already holding the hero prints nothing and records no hit. scripts/mhitu.test.mjs pins all four combinations of the three terms by calling mhitm_ad_phys() directly, and no fresh C case can reach the silent one. Two reasons. The only species whose mattk carries {AT_TUCH, AD_PHYS, 0d0} are the python, the guardian naga and the giant eel's neighbours, all far above monmax_difficulty() on dungeon level 1, which monst.h:259 caps at (level_difficulty() + u.ulevel) / 2; and u.ustuck has to point at that attacker, which needs mon.c set_ustuck()'s AT_HUGS caller, refused at js/mhitu.js:626. Record a case once a monster can grab the hero.

notes.text: The species list above is loose. The five species carrying an {AT_TUCH, AD_PHYS} attack are the quivering blob (difficulty 6), the violet fungus (5), the python (8), the ghost (12) and the guardian naga (17); the giant eel named there has {AT_TUCH, AD_WRAP} instead and does not belong. deferred.detail:
js/allmain.js:686-688 chooses the elapsed turn's message and status seams with `message: planning ? silentMessage : ttyPline` and `statusRefresh: planning ? () => {} : () => bot()`. Replacing the first with `ttyPline` outright leaves the entire suite green: measured at ee6c7c5, `npm test` reported 3970 pass and 0 fail with the substitution in place. The dry run's write is invisible because planningState() spreads the live state, so `_ttyToplines` on the clone is a copied string, and the shared nhDisplay is painted with the same text the live pass writes over immediately afterwards. What it would not survive is a turn whose clone carries `_pending_message`: ttyPline() would then reach dismissPendingTtyMessage() on the shared display and consume a key from the live input queue.

Found while closing nh-timeout-env-seam-untested, whose new cases pin nh_timeout_elapsed_turn()'s seam from both sides and pin preflightSimpleMonsterActions()'s isolation, but cannot reach this call site: finishElapsedTurn() and advanceElapsedTurn() are both module-private to js/allmain.js, and moveloop_core() runs the planning and live passes together.

QUALITY.json already carries a sibling of exactly this obstacle -- the entry noting that ELAPSED_TURN_PLANNING_REFUSALS' three added classes are unpinned because 'advanceElapsedTurn() is not exported, and driving moveloop_core() from that fixture does not reach the arm'. Both close together if the elapsed turn gains a seam a test can drive.

Closing condition: a case that reaches the planning pass through a real turn and fails when js/allmain.js:687 passes ttyPline while planning -- either by giving the elapsed turn a driveable seam, or by a turn whose clone carries a pending message, where the dry run's ttyPline would consume a keystroke the segment still needs. Found by the tests deferral burn-down.

The refusal and the three-in-four fall-through to hitmu() on the rider both have unit coverage in scripts/mounted-move.test.mjs and neither has a recorded C case. scripts/run-mounted-move.mjs now records the non-adjacent half, on seed 6128; the adjacent half needs a seed search that the two seeds this matrix uses do not satisfy. js/teleport.js mnexto() ends by assigning `relocated.mux = state.u.ux; relocated.muy = state.u.uy` as a stand-in for the set_apparxy() call C makes inside rloc_to(). js/monmove.js already exports a ported set_apparxy(), tested by nine cases in scripts/monmove.test.mjs, so the stand-in duplicates code the port has. Commit 2c866f5 re-derived the caller inventory into a comment and stated the precondition, but a comment is all that holds it: a caller whose monster is blind, or one reached while the hero is invisible, displaced or underwater, would take set_apparxy()'s displacement path and spend an rn2 the stand-in does not. Replacing the two assignments with a set_apparxy() call would remove the precondition entirely. It changes production behavior only if some caller does not in fact take an early return, so it needs its own differential across all three callers (js/allmain.js:217, js/dog.js:796, js/do.js:1406) rather than a test-only change; that is why this lane did not do it. Found by the tests deferral burn-down.

scripts/mkroom-shop.test.mjs:826-834 defines a name_wanted() helper transcribed from shknam.c:507-515, and three assertions now compare the port's keeper name against it: the general store pair (commit 2c866f5), the jewelers pair, and the hardware store's notEqual. js/shknam.js nameshk() computes the same expression independently. The two are transcriptions of one C line, so an error shared by both survives every one of those assertions -- for instance `(nseed % 13) - (nseed % 5)` written as `(nseed % 13) - (nseed % 3)` in both places. Closes when at least one case pins the index against a value read from the C source for a stated m_id, ubirthday and ledger_no rather than against a second copy of the formula, the way the new shktools case pins its three indices against literal names. Found by the tests deferral burn-down.

js/eat.js done_eating():1889, `state.context.victual = zero_victual();`, is a mutation survivor. Deleting it leaves all 24 tests in scripts/eat-occupation.test.mjs green, including the two that assert `assert.deepEqual(game.context.victual, zero_victual())` after a meal, and the victual is still fully zeroed at the end of the new two-meal segment. The reason is that done_eating()'s useup(piece) reaches js/invent.js obfree():1677-1680, which calls food_disappears() (js/eat.js:901-903), and that zeroes the same struct one call earlier. C has the same double write -- shk.c obfree():1195-1196 calls eat.c food_disappears(), which assigns zero_victual, and eat.c done_eating():572 assigns it again -- so this is faithful redundancy rather than a defect, and no ported path reaches done_eating() without obfree() running first. The likely right resolution is to record it as a permanent survivor with that reason rather than to chase a test for it; filing it so the next mutation run over js/eat.js does not rediscover it cold. Found by the tests deferral burn-down.

js/exper.js experience()'s repeat-kill loop condition `tmp > 1` yields a permanent mutation survivor that no assertion can kill. `tmp >= 1` returns the same value for every input: tmp is at least 1 on entry, Math.trunc((1 + 1) / 2) is 1, and i and nk are dead after the loop, so the extra iterations change nothing observable. Exhaustive simulation over tmp 1..3000 and nk 0..400, covering the one-byte kill count the caller passes, found no differing pair. Every future mutation run over that line will report it, and each report costs a trace: the deferral mutate-sites-reports-a-false-survivor was opened on exactly that trace. Record the reason where a review will find it, or exclude the site. Found by the tests deferral burn-down.

scripts/mutate-sites.mjs mutates relational operators, `&&`, `||`, boolean literals and integer bounds, so it cannot express dropping a whole disjunct or a statement, which is the defect shape two correctness passes over the melee subsystem kept finding. This is the surviving half of mutate-sites-reports-a-false-survivor, whose other claim did not reproduce, and it is the reason that entry gave for mutation score and test quality being close to uncorrelated in that range: eed732b3..5168910 scored 253 of 220 killed with six real test defects in it, and 5168910..dc31f03 scored 68 of 144 surviving with no production defect. A deletion kind, dropping one operand of `&&` or `||`, would let the number speak to the defects the passes actually find. Costs a new site kind, its enumeration, and its report labels. Found by the tests deferral burn-down.

js/mthrowu.js blocking_terrain():40-41 reads an absent GameMap cell as C's leading !isok(x, y) at mthrowu.c:1284, and the two are not the same set. cmd.c isok():4329 is x >= 1 && x <= COLNO - 1 && y >= 0 && y <= ROWNO - 1, so C rejects column zero; js/game.js GameMap.at():78-81 rejects only x < 0 and x >= COLNO, so column zero has a cell and the port falls through to IS_OBSTRUCTED(levl[0][y].typ). The answers agree today for one reason only: mklev never puts anything but rock in column zero, and IS_OBSTRUCTED(STONE) is TRUE, so both sides answer TRUE. js/const.js:2028 already exports an isok() that matches C exactly; the fix is to call it. Filed as production rather than tests, and filed rather than fixed, because the burn-down lane that found it was forbidden to move production behavior. scripts/mthrowu.test.mjs now covers both coordinates and says which arm each one reaches, so the fix has a test waiting for it. Found by the tests deferral burn-down.

A count of 2 or more before any extcmdlist[] row other than the two carrying occupation text refuses at js/cmd.js rhack(), where cmd.c parse():5142-5144 has left gm.multi above 0. C spends such a count in one of two places, and neither is ported: rhack():3728-3729 installs timed_occupation() for a row with f_text, and allmain.c moveloop_core():515-531 repeats the command for every other row.

Two recorded cases sit just outside the goal and cannot match the C reference yet. Both were recorded at seed 9310001, datetime 20260814101500, a Valkyrie with pettype:none and !acoustics, moves prefixed by the space that dismisses startup output; the count digits are typed at a prompt whose row 0 already reads 'Be careful!  New moon tonight.'.

1. ' 12i'. C paints 'Count: 12' at the second digit and then opens the inventory once: doinv() answers ECMD_OK, so rhack():3814 reaches reset_cmd_vars() and zeroes gm.multi before moveloop_core() can repeat anything. The port stops at the 'i' with 4 of C's 5 screens, its message row still holding 'Count: 12'.
2. ' 3>'. No echo, because get_count():5069 withholds it below 10. C answers 'You can't go down here.' once, again through the ECMD_OK arm. The port stops at the '>' with 3 of C's 4 screens.

Both are correct in C through code this port already owns, so the refusal costs real behavior. It is deliberate: admitting them would send an uncounted command down moveloop_core()'s non-occupation gm.multi > 0 arm, which no recorded session has executed.

scripts/cmd.test.mjs 'a count of 2 or more refuses on a row this port would dispatch' pins the present refusal for both inputs. Close this by moving both into scripts/run-count-prefix.mjs with the slice that ports timed_occupation() and rhack()'s set_occupation() call site, and by extending that matrix with a counted 's' and a counted '.'.

notes.text:
The occupation half of this entry's blocker landed with the slice that commit 8544a59 closes; that slice's js/cmd.js lines were carried into the tree by fc211b3, which staged them by accident. cmd.c timed_occupation() and rhack():3728-3729's set_occupation() call are ported, and scripts/run-count-prefix.mjs now records ' 9s' and ' 3.' against the C reference. deferred.detail:
js/cfgfiles.js config_error_add() keeps the whole message. C truncates twice
before it reaches a screen:

- pline.c vconfig_error_add() formats into a BIGBUFSZ buffer and then writes
  `buf[BUFSZ - 1] = '\\0'`, cutting the message at 255 bytes.
- pline.c vpline() (212-225) cuts anything still longer than BUFSZ - 1 and
  rewrites the tail as `...` plus the final three characters, so a long
  offending line echoed by `pline("\\n%s", origline)` arrives elided rather
  than merely clipped. origline holds up to 4 * BUFSZ bytes, so a
  1023-character configuration line reaches this.

Nothing shorter than 256 bytes can tell the difference, and the recorded
screens truncate at 80 columns anyway, so this shows up only in a message the
port would raw-print onto a second and third row where C prints one. No
development session has such a line; a fresh case would need an rc statement
of its own.

js/options.js stripNegation() steps over whitespace after each negation prefix;
options.c:539-542 does not.

    while ((*opts == '!') || !strncmpi(opts, "no", 2)) {
        opts += (*opts == '!') ? 1 : (opts[2] != '-') ? 2 : 3;
        negated = !negated;
    }

C advances by exactly one, two or three bytes, so `OPTIONS=! time` leaves
opts as " time". optlen is then length_without_val(" time", 5) = 5, and
strncmpi(name, " time", 5) matches no allopt[] row, so the statement is
"Unknown option ' time'." and flags.time keeps its default. The port trims the
space, matches `time` and sets it.

The port's other parseoptions() port, the one doset() reaches
(js/options.js:3905-3911), already strips the prefixes exactly as C does, so
the two disagree with each other as well as with C. Fixing the rc-side one is
a few lines, but it changes which statements match, so it wants its own
development-score check rather than a ride on an unrelated slice. No recorded
session spells a negation this way: a census of the 33 development sessions
finds 67 negated OPTIONS elements over four option names -- autopickup,
legacy, splash_screen and tutorial -- and none carries whitespace after the
prefix.

An OPTIONS statement that reaches one of allopt[]'s two pfx rows without
naming a condition this port recognizes still stops the segment, at
js/options.js applyOption()'s `unported prefix option` refusal.

options.c reaches those rows two ways (556-580): str_start_is() accepts any
suffix of the prefix, and match_optname() accepts a leading substring of the
prefix name itself down to minmatch. So `cond`, `cond_`, `cond_bogus`,
`cond_blind:on`, `font` and `fontbogus:value` all match, and each one then
gets its row's handler. pfxfn_cond_() (options.c:2545-2588) hands the whole
statement to botl.c parse_cond_option(), which answers 1 for a suffix no
condtests[] row matches and 2 for a statement no longer than "cond_", and the
handler reports "Unknown condition option %s (%d)". Because pfx_match is set,
options.c:675-682 then adds a second error, "bad option suffix variation
'%s'", over the statement text truncated at its first colon. pfxfn_font() is
not ported at all.

Two errors from one statement is a shape no other rc path in this port
produces, and the second one needs pfx_match carried out of the match loop.
Until then the refusal is named rather than reported as an unknown option,
which would be the wrong message for every one of these.

Inputs and expected C output, taken from the source above rather than a
recording: `OPTIONS=cond_bogus` gives
" * Line 1: Unknown condition option cond_bogus (1)." followed by
" * Line 1: bad option suffix variation 'cond_bogus'.", and `OPTIONS=cond`
gives only " * Line 1: Unknown condition option cond (2)." because it matched
through match_optname() with pfx_match still false.

notes.text: Two of botl.c parse_status_hl1()'s bounds are unreachable while HILITE_STATUS goes undispatched, and become reachable the day it lands, so the slice that adds the row owes them a case. parseoptions() (options.c:521-525) refuses an element over BUFSZ/2, reporting 'Option too long, max length is 128 characters' before any handler runs, and 'hilite_status:' spends 14 of those 128 bytes. A hilite_status value therefore cannot exceed 114 bytes through OPTIONS, which puts both bounds out of reach: parse_status_hl1()'s per-field 'ccount < QBUFSZ - 2' needs 126 characters in one field, and its 'fldnum < MAX_THRESH' needs 21 '/' separators, at which point parse_status_hl2() reads hsbuf[21], one past the array. Measured at seed 3310277 and 19960229180000: a 163-byte OPTIONS element reported the length error, and a 149-byte one reporting the same error was reduced to 86 bytes to reach the field limit, where C answered "Unknown behavior '<six uninitialized bytes>'". cfgfiles.c has no such cap on a statement's own value, so HILITE_STATUS=... reaches parse_status_hl1() with the whole line. This note records the finding for that slice; status-hilite-rules-still-fail-closed left both bounds ported and untested for the same reason.

Its one reader is cmd.c dotoggleoption() (1376-1384), which hands gc.cmd_bind->param to toggle_bool_option(); with no param stored it prints "Use #optionsfull to set any option instead." instead. Nothing in this port dispatches the #toggle extended command yet, so the store has no consumer and lands with dotoggleoption().

js/options.js statusConditionNames() and parseStatusHiliteRule() throw optionError() for an unknown status condition, alias or threshold, where cfgfiles.c reports a configuration error and reads on. This is the defect class a634c32 fixed for BIND and OPTIONS statements, one subsystem over: a mistyped STATUSHILITE rule costs the whole segment above runSegment()'s catch instead of one line of the error block. Closing it needs no unported C. Found by the fix agent's sweep for unguarded rc-text indexes during the correctness pass over 1842f5e3..a634c32, and not covered by any entry open at that time.

js/options.js ports cmd.c bind_mousebtn() (2623-2659) for its answer alone, so parsebindings() reports and falls through exactly as C does, but the gc.Cmd.mousebtn[] store the C function writes has no JavaScript home. An accepted mouse binding therefore leaves no state behind. Nothing reads that array until mouse input is ported, so the gap changes no observable behavior today; this entry exists so it has a durable record when it does.

js/options.js MENU_HEADING_ATTRIBUTES maps 'dim', 'italic' and 'blink' to ATR_NONE, because recorder patch 006 retains only bold, underline and inverse. That is right for menu_headings, where optfn_menu_headings() stores one attribute, and wrong for a status highlight: botl.c parse_status_hl2():3028-3040 sets HL_DIM, HL_ITALIC or HL_BLINK alongside whatever came before, while ATR_NONE alone reaches 'disp_attrib = HL_NONE', which discards the attributes named earlier in the same action. The port therefore reads 'dim' as that discard.

Measured at seed 3310277 and 19960229180000. OPTIONS=hilite_status:hitpoints/always/bold&dim draws HP with ESC[1m in C and with no attribute in the port, because 'dim' cleared the bold that 'bold' had set. The colour survives either way, so OPTIONS=hilite_status:hitpoints/always/red&italic matches.

Fixing it means separating the two readings: parse_status_hl2() and parse_condition() need an answer that distinguishes a tty-invisible attribute from ATR_NONE, which menuHeadingAttribute() cannot give while it is shared with parseMenuHeadingStyle(). It sits outside status-hilite-rules-still-fail-closed, which ports the error arms.

The port answers Return with "Unknown command '^M'." where C runs a command. js/tty_rawprint.js nomux_raw_putch() stores one screen cell per byte, which is
what recorder patch 006 does, but the recorded screen a byte grid produces is
not a byte grid. The capture writes the shadow buffer's bytes to a file, and
the session loader reads that file as UTF-8, so a two-byte sequence in adjacent
cells arrives as one character and the recorded row is shorter than 80. The
port's cells hold one JavaScript character per byte, and frozen/terminal.js
serializes each cell on its own, so the same sequence arrives as two.

Measured, not inferred. A fresh case at seed 5128094, 20120919081000, over an
rc whose second line is `OPTIONS=zqxjé` matches C on every random-number call
and every cursor and diverges at the first byte of the é: `Cell row 2, column
13 (ch): C "é", JS "Ã"`. The statement echo config_erradd() prints is enough to
reach it, so any non-ASCII byte in an erroring rc line costs the rest of that
row and every row below it.

Nothing in the port decides this on its own: matching C means the cells a
multi-byte sequence occupies have to serialize as one character, and
frozen/terminal.js is judge-owned. The fix is therefore in what the port puts
in the cells, not in how they are written out, and it wants a decision about
what the raw cursor column then counts. No development session has a non-ASCII
rc line.

notes.text: Read at 9a25f0b: the port owes this fix, but it is not a port of any C, which is why it does not fit this goal's closing condition. The measuring chain is closed at both ends: patch 006 stores one char per cell and emits it byte by byte, and frozen/session_loader.mjs:107 reads the session file as UTF-8. AGENTS.md makes the patched C's output the behavior to match and frozen/ is judge-supplied, so neither end can change, and changing the recorder would invalidate every recording including the holdout. js/tty_rawprint.js nomux_raw_putch() is already a faithful line-for-line port that stores a byte per cell because C does. What is missing is a compensation for a lossy capture: place a whole decoded character in one cell and shift the row's tail, while the recorded cursor still counts bytes. There is no C function to name as its closing condition, so if it survives this goal it should be re-scoped as a display-fidelity entry rather than an unported-behavior one.

Derived from the C, not measured: a fresh case cannot isolate it while

notes.text:
Closed. The record names role.c plsel_startup_msg(); no such function exists.
'grep -rln plsel_startup_msg nethack-c/upstream/' exits 1 with no output. The
line numbers 2821 and 2828 are right and the owner is plsel_startmenu(), at

The record also called the defect unwitnessable while
raw-print-splits-a-multibyte-character stands. That is wrong, and the reason it
is wrong is worth keeping: the header is a menu line, and process_menu_window()
hands nomux_putch() one signed char per byte, so every high-bit byte is below 32
there and leaves its shadow cell blank. The recorded observable is therefore
entirely ASCII, unlike tty_raw_print()'s, which patch 006 casts to unsigned
char and stores. A fresh case at seed 4820577, 20340517080910, over an rc whose
only setting is OPTIONS=name:Aardvarkbcdefghijkem with an e-acute, matched every
call, screen and cursor after the fix and diverged at one cell before it.

Closing it cost two more corrections in js/tty_menu.js, both the same C fact:
tty_end_menu() measures and cuts a stored line with strlen(), and
process_menu_window() advances one column per byte. Without them the fix moved
the whole menu window one column instead of matching C.

deferred.detail:
js/tty_menu.js searchItemText() and sourceMenuLineText() both rebuild the line
tty_end_menu() stored and cut it with String.prototype.slice at columns - 2,
which counts UTF-16 code units. wintty.c:2728-2733 writes the NUL at
curr->str[ttyDisplay->cols - 2], a byte offset, and process_menu_window()'s
MENU_SEARCH arm matches its pattern against that cut string.

role.c plsel_startmenu()'s "%.20s", so the stored-line cut is now spelled in
two units inside one file. Only the search and PICK_ONE paths still read the
code-unit form, and they diverge from C only for a stored line over 78 bytes
that also holds a multibyte character -- an object label or fruit name longer

Closes when one helper owns the cut and all three call sites take it.

wintty.c process_text_window() (1808-1833) sends only the first byte of each
line through g_putch() when its high bit is set, and recorder patch 006 strips
that bit before nomux_putch() stores it: a line beginning 0xC3 0xA9 records 'C'
in the first cell and leaves the second as the clear left it.

js/tty_menu.js has two ports of that loop. writeRecorderTtyWindowLine(), which
displayTtyMenuTextWindow() uses for look_here()'s window, models the first-byte
arm. displayTtyTextWindow(), the paged NHW_TEXT variant, draws through
writeStyledText() instead, which has no first-byte arm and now skips a leading
high-bit byte rather than writing 'C' there.

That skip arrived with the commit that made writeStyledText() count bytes,
which the character-selection header needed; before it the same cell held the
whole character and every later cell was one column left, so the arm is newly
wrong in one cell and newly right in the rest. Nothing reaches it: every
NHW_TEXT line the port draws starts with ASCII.

Closes when the two ports of process_text_window()'s loop become one that
carries both the line's attribute and the first-byte arm.

notes.text:
Correction to the first paragraph of `detail`: it names the wrong cell, and
neither port models the arm.

Recorder patch 006 hooks nomux_putch() three times on the path
process_text_window()'s draw loop takes. Both putchar siblings inside the loop
wrap the call as `{ int svx = ttyDisplay->curx; ttyDisplay->curx--;
nomux_putch(*cp); ttyDisplay->curx = svx; }`. The third hook sits inside
g_putch() itself and has no such compensation. The loop increments curx in its
own condition -- `*cp && (int) ++ttyDisplay->curx < (int) ttyDisplay->cols` --
so throughout byte k's body curx stands one column past the column putchar()
prints that byte in. The compensated hooks therefore record byte k in its own
column and the g_putch() hook records one column to the right.

So a line beginning 0xC3 0xA9 leaves the first cell as the clear left it and
records 'C' in the second. The 0xA9 that follows cannot overwrite that 'C':
nomux_putch() takes an int, `*cp` is a signed char, and the guard
`if (!ttyDisplay || ch < 32) return` drops every negative one.

writeRecorderTtyWindowLine() writes the stripped byte at `column + index`,
which is the first cell, and writeStyledText() writes it nowhere. Both are
wrong by one cell in opposite directions, so this entry blesses neither port;
the merged loop it asks for has to place that byte one column to the right of
the byte's own column.

A second divergence between the same two ports, and a second requirement on
the merged loop.

nomux_putch()'s `ch < 32` guard drops a control byte for the same reason it
drops a high-bit one, and neither reaches the shadow grid.
writeRecorderTtyWindowLine() writes every byte below 0x80 through
display.setCell(), control bytes included, so it fills a cell C leaves as the
preceding clear left it. writeStyledText() drops them, through the
`bytes[index] < 0x20` half of its skip; scripts/tty-menu.test.mjs
'process_menu_window emits no cell for a control byte' pins that half.

The merged loop therefore has to drop every byte below 0x20 as well as every
high-bit byte that is not the g_putch() first byte, on top of placing that
first byte in the column named in the note above.

js/dogmove.js conflictActive() at :219 adds a negated blocked conjunct where youprop.h:218 is `#define Conflict (HConflict || EConflict)` with no blocking term. It is the same defect the chunk at d110b39 fixed in heroDeaf() three lines below, and I verified both sides at 132923c: the C macro has two disjuncts, and the port ANDs a third negated term. It is worse than the heroDeaf one, whose reader was dead. This has four readers inside dog_move(), at js/dogmove.js:956, :1008, :1066 and :1072, all on live paths, so a hero whose conflict is blocked would have pets behave as C's unconflicted where C reads the property as set. Closing it needs no unported C: copy youprop.h:218's two-disjunct form, and pin it with a case that sets uprops[CONFLICT].blocked while leaving intrinsic or extrinsic set. Found by the copied-predicates worker, which correctly left it alone as outside the two entries its chunk named.

notes.text: Correction on both scope and severity, from the slice-selector's reading at ea8188f2, which I verified. Scope: the entry names one site and there are five, all adding a negated blocked term to a two-disjunct macro. js/dogmove.js:219; js/mhitm.js:100, whose reader is mhitm.c:436; js/mhitu.js:96 via activeHeroProperty() at :618, whose reader is mhitu.c:803; and js/monmove.js:408 and :424, both propertyActive(state, CONFLICT, true), against monmove.c:1302 and :1318. Four other sites already spell it correctly, at js/mon.js:392, js/monmove.js:1697 and :2597, and js/unported_monster_actions.js:175, which is what makes this one C rule answered two ways rather than a consistent house style. Severity, downgraded: C never blocks CONFLICT, so the extra conjunct cannot change an answer today. youprop.h defines a blocked alias for exactly six properties, at :90 BLINDED, :181 CLAIRVOYANT, :197 INVIS, :209 STEALTH, :239 LEVITATION and :252 FLYING; `grep -rn BConflict nethack-c/upstream/` returns nothing and exits 1; and the only writers are worn.c:38-44 w_blocks(), which yields INVIS, CLAIRVOYANT or BLINDED, and polyself, which sets FLYING, LEVITATION and STEALTH. I read w_blocks() myself and confirm those three are all it can produce. So this is a spelling defect that no input reaches, not the live divergence the original detail implies, and its closing condition should pin all five sites at once.

deferred.detail: js/monmove.js holds two hero-property helpers with identical bodies and opposite defaults, so an omitted third argument answers differently depending on which one a caller happened to pick. propertyActive(state, property, blockedMatters = false) is at :373 and activeProperty(state, property, blockedMatters = true) at :1685; I read both at e7aee5a and the four statements between them are the same. js/unported_monster_actions.js:141 carries a third copy with the true default. CONFLICT is now read through both, at :413, :429 and :2602 through propertyActive and at :1702 through activeProperty with an explicit false, which is what makes the pair reachable rather than theoretical: the chunk at e7aee5a had to know which default each site carried in order to drop a term from five of them. Closing it needs no unported C. One helper spelling per property class is what youprop.h describes, since a property either has a blocked alias or does not, and the caller should not choose. Pin it by giving each C property its own predicate named for the macro, the convention js/display.js:2946-2958 records and js/mhitm.js and js/mhitu.js now follow for Conflict, then delete both general helpers. Found by the conflict-gets-one-spelling worker, which correctly left it alone as outside the entry its chunk named.

A female monster does not: js/display.js presentedMonsterGlyphInfo() and actualMonsterGlyphInfo() build a monster presentation without glyphflags, and nothing sets MG_FEMALE from monst->female the way display.h mon_to_glyph() (554-556) picks GLYPH_MON_FEM_OFF and reset_glyphmap()'s GLYPH_MON_FEM_OFF arm raises the bit.

Reachability: wizard mode only, so playmode:debug. It was already reachable from a configuration file before this slice, because 'wizmgender' is a set_wizonly BoolOpt that parseoptions() accepts; what this slice adds is the menu path, since optfn_boolean()'s seven-option arm no longer refuses. No development session runs in debug mode with a female monster on screen, so nothing measures it today.

Closing it needs a glyph number for the monster ranges, which is the same conversion the terrain slice makes for cmap. Inputs for a case: playmode:debug, OPTIONS=wizmgender, a female monster in sight, then toggle 'wizmgender' from the full 'mO' menu; C inverts the monster's cell and this port does not.

notes.text: Closed at 2aab973, and the remedy this entry recorded was wrong. It said closing needed a glyph number for the monster ranges, the same conversion the terrain slice made for cmap. No C writer ever puts a monster number into levl[x][y].glyph: display.c:284, :302, :319, :359, :361, :436 and :555 store cmap, object, trap or engraving numbers, bones.c:569 stores GLYPH_UNEXPLORED, mkmaze.c:1840 a cmap number, ball.c's nine sites copy a number another writer produced, and the one exception, map_invisible() at :382, stores the constant GLYPH_INVISIBLE, whose arm raises MG_INVIS and no gender bit. detect.c:2205-2209 states the rule in a comment. Monsters reach the screen through gg.gbuf, and docrt_flags() rebuilds that buffer by re-running newsym() over every monster, so the repaint re-derives each monster cell whether or not it is numbered. The actual closing condition was carrying MG_FEMALE and MG_MALE on the live-drawn presentations and running win/tty/wintty.c tty_print_glyph()'s three-arm chain over them in C's order, at 208 changed lines rather than a range conversion. Recorded so the closed entry does not preserve the refuted remedy for a later reader.
