hack.c domove_bump_mon():1934-1936 admits its arm when `svc.context.nopick && !svc.context.travel && (canspotmon(mtmp) || glyph_is_invisible(glyph) || glyph_is_warning(glyph))`. js/hack.js requireNoMonsterBump() carries the canspotmon() disjunct alone. The warning disjunct is constantly false, because no ported path raises a warning level, but the marker one stopped being false when mhitm.c pre_mm_attack() gained a writer for it in this slice.

C prints "Pardon me, <pet>." or "You move right into <mon>." and spends the turn. The port falls through to hack.c domove_attackmon_at() and uhitm.c attack_checks(), whose `attacking an unseen monster` refusal (js/uhitm.js:307) stops the segment on the same screen C would have printed over, so this is a fail-closed stop rather than a silent divergence. What it costs is the owner named on the stop.

To reach it: a monster the hero cannot spot standing on a square whose map memory already holds the marker -- the pet must have fought it there and it must not have moved -- with the 'm' prefix pressed at it. Fresh-matrix seed 4310374 leaves a marker with a live monster under it, so the setup exists; no recorded case presses the prefix at one.

js/mon.js mondead() forgets the invisible-monster marker through display.c unmap_object(), which throws UnsupportedMapMemoryError for a seenv CORR, ICE or ROOM square that carries an engraving. On the live elapsed-turn scan that class reaches nobody: js/allmain.js advanceElapsedTurn() converts a refusal only in the catch around preflightSimpleMonsterActions(), and the live movemon() loop below it has a finally and no conversion, so the error escapes moveloop_core() and runSegment() and the segment loses its whole matching prefix instead of ending on its last matching screen.

The port relies on the plan discovering every refusal the live pass would raise. This is the one place that guarantee is now broken, and the correctness pass over 389a8a2..16d4e33 is what found it. js/mhitm.js pre_mm_attack() marks through a seam the plan binds to a no-op, because display.c map_invisible() writes map memory and then paints through show_glyph_cell(), which takes no state and paints the module-global game. So the plan sees no marker where the live pass writes one, and a monster dying on that square reaches unmap_object() only on the live pass.

Two ways to close it, both needing a recorded case first. Give the live movemon() loop in advanceElapsedTurn() the same class conversion the preflight catch has, so any live-scan refusal ends the segment on its last matching screen; or split map_invisible() into its memory and paint halves so the plan can mirror the live pass on isolated cells, which removes the divergence rather than handling it. The second is closer to what the planning clone is for, and more work. UnsupportedMapMemoryError is already in elapsedTurnPlanningRefusals(), so the planning half of the pair is handled.

No development session reaches it: it needs an engraving on the square where a monster the hero cannot spot is killed by another monster. Closing it needs a fresh recording of that square.

dig.c rot_corpse() (2158-2166) writes "Your <corpse> rots away" through corpse_xname() and can reach remove_worn_item() and stop_occupation() when the rotting corpse's where is OBJ_INVENT; js/timeout.js unportedDueTimerReason() refuses the whole turn instead, and the OBJ_MINVENT and OBJ_MIGRATING arms beside it refuse the same way. Representative case just outside the ported OBJ_FLOOR arm: seed 334, datetime 20000110090000, rc OPTIONS=name:FreshDiff,role:Healer,race:human,gender:male,align:neutral,!legacy,!tutorial,!splash_screen and OPTIONS=pettype:none,time, moves 'b ,b\r' followed by 235 'm.' rests -- step onto the pile at <52,17>, take the elf corpse (menu letter b), then wait for turn 236. Expected failure today: the port stops with 'a corpse on the floor, but one is rotting at where=3'. The case cannot be recorded as it stands, because the arrow trap at <52,17> stops the port earlier with 'unsupported hero move: trap activation'; a seed whose visible corpse sits on an untrapped square would carry it.

js/allmain.js advanceElapsedTurn() now converts UnsupportedHeroTimeoutBoundaryError around its finishElapsedTurn() call, so a refusal the live monster scan creates ends the segment on its last matching screen instead of escaping runSegment(). Nothing pins that conversion: deleting the catch leaves the whole suite green.

The correctness pass over 6f718ac..0d5e197 found the escape and traced the path. mon.c mpickstuff() is ported, and its corpse filter at js/monmove.js:2090-2097 (mon.c:1875-1880) lets an M1_COLLECT monster take an acidic or petrifying corpse off the floor; the corpse's ROT_CORPSE element stays in the queue at the same expiry, because js/obj.js calls obj_timer_checks() only for a nonzero `timed` and that function acts only on ice. So a turn the pre-turn preflight admitted reaches run_timers() with the corpse at OBJ_MINVENT, which it refuses. Only the unburdened path is exposed: a burdened hero's clone runs the whole once-per-turn block and refuses first.

What a test needs is a monster that actually reaches mpickstuff()'s carry arm inside one turn. Two fixtures were tried and neither did. A hostile gnome standing on an acid blob corpse never reaches the arm, because mpickstuff() runs from postmov(), after a move. A gnome placed one square further out, so the corpse lies between it and the hero, did not move at all: it ended the turn on its starting square with an empty pack while the corpse rotted normally. A gnome's speed is 6 against NORMAL_SPEED 12, so it acts every other turn, and the fixture drives only one; a faster M1_COLLECT species, two turns, or a recording would each answer that.

Closing this needs one of those, and the recording is worth preferring: the case is a hostile picking a corpse off the floor on the turn that corpse comes due, which is ordinary play rather than a constructed state.

deferred.detail:
js/vision.js vision_reset() opens with `if (!level) return;`, so a caller that hands it something without a `level` gets silence instead of an error. Every one of block_point(), unblock_point() and recalc_block_point() is that same rebuild, so the guard covers the whole vision-index surface.

hero-pushes-a-boulder found the cost. js/obj.js passes its lifecycle env, not a state, as the third argument to the blockPoint and recalcBlockPoint hooks, so wiring `blockPoint: block_point` directly makes vision_reset(env) see no env.level and return without doing anything. The transparency index then never learns about the pushed boulder, and seed0004 diverges at step 212, where C draws rn2(2 + boulderspots) from mthrowu.c linedup() precisely because the new boulder blocks the line. The correct wiring is `(x, y, env) => block_point(x, y, env.state)`. Four test files carried the same silent no-op before it was found, and the slice's own worker reports the diagnosis cost about an hour.

Nothing failed while the wiring was wrong. The guard turned a wiring error into a screen mismatch 22 steps downstream of the call, which is the failure mode AGENTS.md ranks worst: a silently skipped effect rather than a named stop.

Closing this means deciding what the guard is for. If no caller may legitimately pass a state without a level, it should throw rather than return, the way js/display.js see_nearby_objects() refuses a foreign state. If some caller does, that caller should be named in a comment and the rest should throw. Either way the hook's argument shape should be pinned by a test, since the current one passes with the hook bound to a function that does nothing.

js/mklev.js makelevel() (401) has no counterpart to mklev.c:1267's `slev = Is_special(&u.uz); if (slev && !Is_rogue_level(&u.uz)) makemaz(slev->proto);`, and does not import Is_special from js/dungeon.js, where the function exists at :1261. A level change that lands on a des-file level therefore builds an ordinary random level in silence, where C builds the special one from its .lua prototype.

This is a live divergence rather than a refusal, which AGENTS.md ranks worse than a named stop: nothing fails, and the first evidence is a screen mismatch on the arrival.

It was found while capping candidates for the goal ranking at 6926a7b, and it is what caps level_tele()'s print_dungeon() menu at 4 steps rather than 96. Three development sessions reach it, and each one's first menu pick is such a level: y - Bar-strt: 16 at seed0373 step 44, and e - bigrm: 12 at seed0383 step 43 and seed2600 step 21, all confirmed from the recorded menu pages and the arrival status lines (Home 1, Dlvl:12).

Closing it means porting the dispatch and enough of makemaz() to build one prototype, or refusing the branch by name so a special-level arrival stops instead of drawing an ordinary level. The refusal is the smaller change and would convert three silent divergences into three named stops; the port is what those three sessions actually need.

- The leading count (read.c:3154-3161) and the out-of-range quantity it can produce (3165-3166, which needs monster_census()). Input: `^G`, `2 gas spore`, Return. C makes two.
- The six gear, state and gender words searched for anywhere in the answer (3169-3193): "saddled ", "sleeping ", "invisible ", "hidden ", "female ", "male ". Each sets a request field create_particular_creation() acts on with put_saddle_on_mon(), mtmp->msleeping, MM_MINVIS, mtmp->mundetected, or an explicit gender that can raise d->genderconf and take the 3291-3311 arm. Input: `^G`, `sleeping newt`, Return.
- The three disposition prefixes (3197-3206), which reach tamedog() and set_malign(). Input: `^G`, `tame jackal`, Return.
- The wizard-only random arm (3208-3211) and rndmonst() behind it. Input: `^G`, `*`, Return.
- mondata.c name_to_monclass() and its four arms (3231-3246), which js/mondata.js:1181 already records as unported. This is where an unknown name, a class letter and an empty answer all land. Inputs: `^G`, `F`, Return; and `^G`, Return alone, which C sends round create_particular()'s retry loop instead.
- create_particular_creation()'s y_n() force-the-species override (3262-3272), for a species cant_revive() substitutes. Input: `^G`, `shopkeeper`, Return. C offers "Creating human zombie instead; force shopkeeper?".
- create_particular()'s retry loop itself (3390-3403): "I've never heard of such monsters.", "Try again (type * for random, ESC to cancel).", the " [type name or symbol]" prompt extension and thats_enough_tries. No answer can reach it while the parse refuses rather than answering FALSE, so it needs the arms above first.

Expected failure today: each input ends the segment at the command seam with the port's refusal message, after getlin() has echoed the whole typed name. None appears in scripts/run-wizard-genesis.mjs, because a fresh recording cannot pass through a refusal; scripts/wizard-genesis.test.mjs pins each refusal by its message instead.

One further bound on the same prompt is not read.c's. js/makemon_create.js assertSupportedSpecies() admits only the species bands level generation has been verified for, and ^G is the first command that lets a player name any species at all, so a plain name outside those bands -- `^G`, `jabberwock`, Return -- stops with UnsupportedMonsterCreationError even though the parse accepted it. Widening that allowlist is a separate piece of work from the arms above and needs its own differential per species family.

A hero-aimed fire ray that reaches the hero without bouncing first stops one call past this goal's current boundary, at zap.c zhitu():4434 `if (!rn2(3)) (void) destroy_items(&gy.youmonst, AD_FIRE, orig_dam);`, which js/zap.js zhitu() raises UnsupportedZapError('destroy_items() and ignite_items() for the burning hero') for.

The reproducible case, recorded with the C reference at 20260817 and replayed with scripts/diff-fresh.mjs. Seed 20260817, datetime 20260817120000, and the same rc scripts/run-ray-zap.mjs builds:

  OPTIONS=name:RayDown,role:Wizard,race:human,gender:female,align:neutral,playmode:debug
  OPTIONS=!legacy,!tutorial,!splash_screen
  OPTIONS=pettype:none,!acoustics
  OPTIONS=symset:DECgraphics

Moves: Ctrl-W, `wand of fire`, Return, then `zn>`.

Expected failure today: C records 18 steps and the port emits 17. C's step 17 is "The bolt of fire hits you!  Your cloak smoulders!--More--" at cursor [57,0,1], with the hero's own square drawing S_lslant in CLR_ORANGE. The port stops before that screen, because the bolt reaches the hero on its first square -- dobuzz() forces the range to 1 for a bolt with no horizontal delta -- so only two messages precede the boundary, both fit on the top line, and nothing raises a --More-- that would end the segment one message earlier. The recorded log for that step is rn2(19), rn2(7), rn2(20), d(6,6), two rn2(5) from burnarmor(), then rn2(3)=0 at zhitu():4434 and the destroy_items() and maybe_destroy_item() draws behind it.

The matrix in scripts/run-ray-zap.mjs deliberately does not carry this segment, because a fresh differential cannot pass through a refusal. Its first case reaches the same zhitu() arm through a bounce, which raises the --More-- one message earlier and lands inside the boundary instead.

What closes it: the slice fire-destroys-the-heros-potions, which owns zap.c destroy_items() (5964-6097) and maybe_destroy_item() (5797-5954) for the hero, and potion.c potionbreathe() (1931-2118) behind them. js/zap_destroy_items.js already carries the OBJ_MINVENT half of both.

js/zap.js dobuzz() carries C's  from zap.c:4824-4825, and no test pins it: changing the 1 to a 2 leaves the whole suite green, and the goal's correctness pass over 2d84dfa..2325a5b confirmed that by running it.

The pass proposed counting nh_delay_output() frames for a forced-miss vertical bolt and asserting exactly one. The orchestrator tried that fix and it does not discriminate: under the range = 2 mutant a vertical bolt still draws one frame and still prints its miss message once. Two oracles were measured, the animation frame count and the number of 'The bolt of fire whizzes by you!' lines in the accumulated top-line buffer, and both answer the same under 1 and under 2.

That leaves a structural question this slice did not settle. In C the assignment is load-bearing: the bolt does not advance when dx and dy are both zero, so a range above 1 would re-enter the hero-square block and print again. The port's loop ends after one square anyway, which means something else in js/zap.js dobuzz() -- the  return, or an earlier exit -- is doing work C gives to . No reachable input separates the two today, because ubuzz() is the only entry and every vertical zap it makes has range 1. Closing this means finding what ends the port's loop, confirming it matches C's own reason, and either writing the oracle that discriminates or recording at the site that the mutant is equivalent and why.

notes.text: Two gaps the shell ate out of the entry above, restored here. The line the entry is about is the assignment "if (dx === 0 && dy === 0) range = 1;" in js/zap.js dobuzz(), which ports zap.c:4824-4825. And the candidate the last paragraph names for ending the port's loop early is the statement "range += await zap_over_floor(...)" inside that loop, whose return value C uses as a range modifier.

deferred.detail:
js/display.js _statusVitals() reads the hit-point total through _statusHitPoints(), which carries botl.c:141-142's clamp of a negative total to zero, and no oracle in the project separates the clamped call from the unclamped `u.uhp || 0` it replaced. The goal's closing correctness pass found this, and the orchestrator measured it rather than reasoning about it: reverting that one call site to `u.uhp || 0` leaves the full suite green at 4,329 tests and the development score identical at 10 of 33 sessions.

The reason is structural. Of the three renderers that read _statusHitPoints(), _vitalStatusFields() at :3940 and the field at :4382 put the number on a drawn screen, and both witnesses of the-fatal-bolt-says-you-die pin those: seed5002 needs HP:0(12) with u.uhp at -18, seed0103 HP:0(16) with u.uhp at -9. _statusVitals() is different. Nothing draws its string; its two readers, _statusLine2Configuration()'s build() and _statusLine3HungerPrefix(), use only its length, to decide an abbreviation level and a column. A negative total is two characters longer than the clamped zero, and the thresholds those readers compare against move in two-character steps, so the difference cancels for every status line the project builds.

The clamp stays, because it is what botl.c does before every use of the value and removing it would make the port's three renderers disagree with each other for no reason. What is missing is a case that separates them. Closing this means finding a status line whose length sits exactly where two characters change the abbreviation level or the condition column, and asserting that level or column with a negative hit-point total; or establishing that no such line exists, in which case the right record is a comment at the call site saying the clamp there is for consistency with the drawn renderers rather than for any screen.

That distinction matters beyond this line. The last four correctness passes each found their sharpest defect in a value with no operator a mutation run can reach, and this is one: a clamp is not an operator a boolean, logical or relational mutant can change, and the run over this range reported js/display.js:3714 as an equivalent survivor for the same reason.

This port's glyph buffer cannot answer them. show_glyph_cell() (js/display.js:2042) stores a resolved presentation on the cell rather than a number, and only map_glyphinfo() puts a glyph number on a presentation, at js/display.js:1733. Every monster presentation is built by glyphPresentation() (js/display.js:713) instead -- hero_glyph_info(), monster_glyph_info(), presentedMonsterGlyphInfo(), riddenMonsterGlyphInfo(), detectedMonsterGlyphInfo(), mimickedMonsterGlyphInfo() and warningGlyphInfo() -- and carries no number, and map_glyphinfo() has no monster arm to resolve one either (mapGlyphinfoResolves(), js/display.js:1560-1565). So a square showing a monster or a warning answers nothing, and glyph_is_monster() cannot separate the disguise the hero has seen through from the one they have not.

js/zap.js bhit() therefore raises UnsupportedBhitError('glyph_at()') for an M_AP_OBJECT mimic in the flight path, above the arm that would decide it, and pinned by scripts/bhit.test.mjs 'bhit() refuses a mimic disguised as an object'.
